text: They hope that by working with the elected MPs, the elected councillors of the Town Council, they could join us in ensuring that our resources are maximised for the good of our residents.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: These efforts may seem small, particularly, when compared against huge movements or organisations, such as national-level agencies, like the People's Association.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: However, they have given my party colleagues and I invaluable insight and a chance to explore these additional facets of the community and to get to know our people better as their elected representatives.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I also hope that this trickle will eventually bring us to more collaborations, more acceptance that political diversity is important and here to stay.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Community partners should eventually see us as nodes through which we will help our communities overcome challenges, fix problems and grow beyond their current limitations.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Ultimately, my hope is that this leads to a shift toward working for a country that is ultimately better able to adapt to myriad challenges.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And as I have mentioned earlier, while knowing our strengths is key, we also have to sit with our limitations to truly see our flaws candidly.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This can be discomforting, even raw and terrifying.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: But this honesty and ability to sit with our past and current shortcomings is how we enable our growth as a country to happen.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I believe that it is not just about whether it is "me first" or "we first", but "us together".

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We have spoken about the Government's planned evolution from "me first" to "we first" here.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The Government has rightly, like any sensible government, spoken about national security, nimble economy and increased assurance at every stage of life.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: But what I hope to add is a recognition of why "me first", as an ideology emerged amidst the wider formation of our nation.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We have moved from the first formal residence hundreds of years ago to informal immigration from the region and our merger and de-merger with Malaysia.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I have noticed, too, that "me first" is often said to be a natural response to our highly financialised and immigration-centric society and economy: owning the fanciest cars, getting the top MNC jobs, owning freehold landed property as a means of overcoming the constraints of the country that we live in.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Yet we are always told that everything around us will change, everything is insecure, we risk losing it all.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And under this cloud of scarcity, leaving out "me first", it is no wonder that we often see this response as greed, selfishness, sharp elbows, no care for the weak in the society, no care for those without a voice, no care for the planet we share.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Our response to this less-than-ideal state is not to be anti-immigrant or anti-capitalist, particularly as our country has been built of an environment that is the opposite of that.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Heritage should be kept alive, including our schools, community spaces, natural spaces that we and our parents went to.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We should stem the erasure of community heritage currently perceived to be under threat from forces, such as rent and high operating costs.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Our non-physical cultures in the form of languages, arts, hobbies need to be supported as they are threatened by "me first" ideology.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The Government also paints a tender picture of a community where the opposite of "me first" comprises citizens who give up seats on trains, taking initiatives.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: But there are also things which the Government should not directly try to affect.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Using the analogy of a garden, we should note the symbiotic interactions between those living in it, the harmony between macrofauna and microfauna, down to tiny insects, and the essential interactions in the soil to help a garden thrive.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: As policy-maker and enforcer of the law, the Government plays the role of a gardener who occasionally pulls out infestations, provides bigger plots and waters the plants during times of drought.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Having good intentions to prune carefully and balance fertiliser and pest control is essential, but not enough.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The Government must also support the garden to grow, to allow it space to breathe.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We must have reliable, physical and intangible spaces within the garden, combined with accessible ways of moving, that allow people to meet one another, like the void decks of old.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: How can we have a target population for a garden when we have not made space for denizens to discover themselves and grow?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Stop worrying overly about the precise shape of our community.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We must trust that by removing barriers, the inherent wisdom of a population with a mindset of abundance will eventually guide itself to an ever-evolving system that encourages us to flourish together.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Thank you very much for the support you have given me and my WP colleagues in recent years.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Besides serving constituents, in this term of Parliament, we will continue to diligently carry out the mandate that Singaporeans have entrusted to us.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: In the legislative process, we will continue necessary governance oversight, and checks and balances.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: As one of the few opposition voices in a chamber dominated by one party, our responsibility is even greater.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This year marks the 60th anniversary of independence.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: As Singaporeans, we should be proud of the achievements we have achieved together and feel fortunate for our success.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Singapore, whether after independence, during the colonial period, or even earlier, has always been a society that accommodates various ethnic groups, religious beliefs, languages and cultures.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Mutual respect, integration and maintaining an open attitude are the foundations behind Singapore's success.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Facing turbulent and uncertain externality, we need to cherish our diversity even more, which allows us to communicate and have dialogue with people of different positions and find space for cooperation.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We hope for sincere exchange and learn from it.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: What is needed is mutual tolerance, humble listening, honest sharing and seeking common ground whilst respecting differences, rather than deliberate avoidance or unnecessary reservations, and certainly not one-sided discourse.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: After all, a gentleman seeks harmony but not uniformity, whilst a petty person seeks uniformity but not harmony.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Forcing others to accept oneself does not necessarily lead to greater harmony or inclusiveness.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: In an unpredictable environment, what is needed is bold thinking and bridge-building.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We must understand that diversity is strength, not fearsome opposition or division to be feared.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Singapore needs confidence, courage and magnanimity to face multi-faceted reality head-on.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: For Singaporeans of different backgrounds, the key should not be whether national consciousness is proclaimed verbally, but rather seeking understanding, giving each other support and encouragement, and working together to move forward.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: (In English): Finally, the health of our governance institutions, as a reminder of what we must do to set us on a path for an even brighter tomorrow.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Singapore is safe, stable and in many ways, successful.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: But as the saying goes, "past performance is not a guarantee of future success".

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: It is timely to ask if we have the right governance processes to safeguard these outcomes in the long term.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We do so because these are real important mechanisms for any nation to ensure that its future stability and gains are protected for many generations to come.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: They are not perfect, but they are designed to hold back the worst excesses, even when politics get heated.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I wish the new Government all the best and success for delivering for Singapore because that is good for all of us.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: For while we may disagree on approaches, policies, implementation of economic strategies, the one thing that truly unites all of us here is the staunch belief that we will see Singapore succeed.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And for that, all of us here in this House should hold our heads high as we work for the betterment of Singapore, for the safety and the future of those whom we love, more than love itself.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It is my honour to stand here for the first time in this House and I want to first thank the voters of Chua Chu Kang group representation constituency (GRC) for the opportunity to represent them in this 15th Parliament.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Since joining politics, my life has changed in different ways.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: My daughter has observed that my eyebags have their own eyebags.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I have less time to play football with my friends on Sundays.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And even when I do, I am the most polite of players.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: When I get kicked on the back of the leg, I am the first to say, "Sorry, sorry".

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Life is different now, but my family keeps me going.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, I want to start by thanking all of them: my wife, my brother, my kids and my mother, who even comes to volunteer with me at my MPS.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: My family makes me feel that I am part of a team.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I have always believed in the power of a team.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In my public service career, I have changed roles every three to five years.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, often, I had to learn a new job from scratch.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And so, I could never assume I had all the answers and therefore, my approach has always been to lean on the strengths of those in my team – so that together, we are more than the sum of the individual parts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As a political leader, my role is to make decisions on behalf of people.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: My approach is to be inclusive, to create space for voices to be heard and to build trust.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This way, even issues that are divisive can be opportunities to build bridges.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As Transport Minister, I have the chance to put this philosophy into practice.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As you can expect, people give me feedback all the time.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And this is a privilege because, actually, they are telling me their stories and every story is personal – the young couple who wants to buy a car, but finds it out of reach; a single mother who uses her personal mobility scooter to bring her three kids to preschool, even though she knows it is illegal; an office worker who ran in the rain, to catch her bus, but she just missed it; and a father splurging on a private car ride, so that he can get home in time to see his children before they go to bed.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Hearing these stories, I understand why some people feel that the system is sometimes not working for them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: They feel the hard edge of the policy.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: They feel they are on the wrong side of the line.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I would solve every one of these individual problems, if I could, because these are not just matters of efficiency.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: These are matters of fairness and of dignity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But in a compact country like ours, transport needs necessarily collide.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Everyone wants a bus stop just below their homes, but no one wants a bus that stops every 20 metres.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In transport, trade-offs are unavoidable and yet, they are felt deeply and personally.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And that is why it does not just matter what we do.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It matters how we do it, and how we bring people along.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And that is why my approach to policies will be to explain our considerations openly and honestly.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: What we give up, what we gain and why.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Here, I have found that a personal touch really matters.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: A face-to-face meeting, a phone call, or a personal email that I write myself.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Most Singaporeans, when I engage them this way, they are reasonable and fair, even when they disagree with the decision.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Over time, I hope to win more people's trust.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I know trust is won over time, with consistency of action and purpose.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I must show that our processes are fair and my intentions are right.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, my approach is to be open and transparent, and thus, I welcome the Leader of Opposition, Mr Pritam Singh's earlier comments about how the WP will scrutinise the work of the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Rail Reliability Taskforce.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In fact, I will welcome questions from all of us here in this Chamber because good questions are not the sole province of the opposition, but is the responsibility of all of us.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This openness will help me build trust and with trust, the toughest compromises become possible.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But nature groups feared that the soil investigation drilling would harm the fragile ecosystem of the nature reserve.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And so, they amassed in opposition and they pushed back.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But the important thing was both sides continued showing up and this gave us the time to hear each other out.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In the end, nobody got everything that they wanted.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But most importantly, we built trust and as trust grew, stronger solutions for Singapore emerged.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: When I returned to MOT a few months ago, my nature group combatants, turned comrades, were the first to welcome me back, as friends.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: That experience has guided me since then – that trust can be built even when disagreements cut deep but only if we all commit to staying at the table, with the right heart and the right intent.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And that is the spirit I want to bring to shape our transport future.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We want to engage more Singaporeans than ever before – commuters, drivers, cyclists, seniors, persons with disabilities, mobility device users.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We want to bring all of them together to have deeper conversations and to weigh trade-offs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: My hope is simple: that more Singaporeans feel that the system works for them and that their story matters.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Building common ground helps us balance today's needs but it does not solve tomorrow's problems.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: To ease the pressures of zero-sum choices, we must create new ground – new choices, new capacity, new options and possibilities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The older ones amongst us will remember that it was almost impossible to get a taxi on a Friday night or on a rainy day.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: With more cars and flexible fares, more Singaporeans could access door-to-door transport, on a pay per use basis, rather than having to drive or to use or to purchase a car.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Initially, taxi drivers feared that private hire cars would undercut them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But in fact, both sets of drivers benefited from more business and higher earnings If back then, the Government had blocked the entry of Uber and Grab, we would all have been worse off.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Imagine a safe ride home, after a late night out; imagine a doorstep pick-up, to the polyclinic for your medical check-up; imagine doing emails or listening to a podcast in a car, without having to drive; imagine new and exciting jobs for our people, especially our young.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: New possibilities open up when we focus on creation, rather than division.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In sea and air transport, we have done the same.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We dreamt up possibilities that did not exist before, like the world's largest automated port, like our now-iconic Jewel.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We are summoning the same spirit of creation for our economy.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Gan spoke about the Economic Strategy Review.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I co-chair the Committee on Global Competitiveness with Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our Committee comprises a new generation of Singaporean business leaders, who know what it takes to survive and to thrive in today's world.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: All of us share a deep sense of urgency.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We see how the world may be moving against us.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For decades, Singapore benefited from globalisation and free trade.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But as the President explained in his address and as Deputy Prime Minister has explained in his speech, the rules have shifted.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Larger economies are raising tariffs and subsidising their core industrial champions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As a small country, we cannot match them dollar-for-dollar, land-for-land.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This is a big risk, but it is also an opportunity to retool, to move into spaces where others hesitate, to attract new industries for Singapore and create new jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We joined up seven islands to create Jurong Island, to build a petrochemical hub.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We invested in semi-conductors when others felt that we could succeed.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We grew our biomedical industry from washing test tubes to producing vaccines.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And we even built a world-class integrated resort, on land reclaimed from the sea.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: These were not just about maintaining the status quo.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And now, it is time for us to do it again.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Not everything will succeed but if just one, two or three of these bets come good, they will transform our economy and carry Singapore to the next level.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: What matters most is whether Singaporeans can step into these new opportunities that we create.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: With a faster pace of economic change, people will have more career transitions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Fewer people will climb a single career ladder like I did, almost did.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Most will have multiple jobs, move across many jobs and industries across their lifetimes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Career transitions can be unsettling if faced alone.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Of course, a career change can feel daunting.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In these moments, a word of encouragement, a gesture of care can make all the difference.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: When I decided to join politics, I felt unsettled, too.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I was a civil servant and I did not know how I would fare under public scrutiny and politics was a whole new ballgame.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In April, I had to make my first political speech.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I remember rehearsing in a corner, slightly nervously.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We did not know each other very well before, but he came over, he placed his hands on my shoulders and said, "As long as you are doing the right thing, do not worry about what other people say." His words made all the difference to me that day.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It gave me the strength to step forward and to speak like a lion.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: To unlock the full potential of Singaporeans, we must support one another.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: When friends and family try new things, celebrate them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Treat others' success as if they were our own.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Because when one of us rises, all of us rise together.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Someone who wants to create what has yet to be imagined.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Someone who believes that we achieve more when we work together.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: They will always have my support and I hope they will have yours, too.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Not long ago, I read a letter that was published in the Lianhe Zaobao.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It was titled "请把父亲还给我", or please return my father to me.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: When she asked him if work was more important than family, he replied, "The company needs me.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I have to do it." At the end of her letter, she wrote, "家庭，才是人生最不该错过的末班车".

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Family is the last bus in life that we must never miss.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It reminded me of my own relationship with my father.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: He, too, worked long hours in a coffee shop.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Growing up, I wished for his presence even though I understood his absence.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Now, I find myself feeling the same tensions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Some evenings, my children would see me heading out.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: They would ask, "Where are you going, Daddy?" I wonder in those moments, if I am giving them enough.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: They do not need me to tuck them into bed anymore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But they still need me to listen, to be present and to show up.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The way forward is together, with our families, our friends and as one nation, because the meaningful things in life cannot be done alone.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong, do you have a clarification?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: First, the Deputy Prime Minister said there was a 5% above-trend growth scenario, which was going to be driven by high-growth sectors.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: What is the composition of reskilled labour and new labour input?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: If the Deputy Prime Minister has those assumptions driving the model?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: My second question is, there has been an increasing number of AI labs setting up here, like Mistral and Google.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: I understand that they have been accorded incentives.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: What are the report cards for these incentives accorded to them?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The third question, given that both Ministers have mentioned space, is that I noticed there is no space agency here.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Are those your three clarifications to one of the Ministers and no more clarifications?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I thought that there were no more clarifications, I almost left.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Anyway, I am glad to have the questions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Exactly what skills we will need is something that we will have to work through with the industries that we are promoting.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When we bring in the industries, they will need new skills, new workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Existing workers have to be upskilled, have to be retrained.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is something that we have to also prepare ahead of time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Even as we negotiate and discuss with new industries coming in, we will already start talking about the type of workers that they need, the type of skills that they need.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some of the industries that we bring in may already exist in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They may be upgrading their production, upgrading their operations, moving into higher value-added activities.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In that case, they may also need to upgrade their workers who are already in their companies.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is a combination of new workers and existing workers upgrading, new skills.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will be an entire transformation that we will need to go through.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is part and parcel of our tripartite efforts.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We work with companies, we work with our trade unions, our worker representatives to see how we can support their skills upgrading and retraining journey.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First, at the broad level, we would like to encourage companies to embrace AI technology so that their workers at all levels are familiar with the use of AI and confident in using AI-enabled tools going forward.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is a little bit like digitalisation previously, where we wanted to encourage all our workers to be digitally ready so that they are comfortable with using digital tools.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Similarly for AI, at the first level, we want to have a broad adoption and acceptance of AI technology and skills.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the second level, within the companies, for companies that are bigger, we want to encourage them to invest in building up AI capability within the company.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are what we call company-based AI centres of excellence.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We support them, we encourage them, we help them, we give them grants so that they are able to build up their AI capability.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They will take some time for them to be able to familiarise with and to be able to be confident in building up their AI centres of excellence.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the third level, there are also a lot of companies that are much smaller.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They do not have the confidence to be able to build company-based AI centres of excellence.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, they want to be able to tap on some national platforms.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is why we also have national, sectoral-based AI centres of excellence.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: One example is in manufacturing, which we have already set up.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We make that facility available to manufacturing companies, to tap on this capacity so that they can build their AI capability.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Once they are familiar and confident, if they want to build our own company-based AI centre of excellence, they can do so, as and when they are ready.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is why we are also focusing on developing our space industry in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We do want to explore the different possibilities and opportunities in space technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: It is the story of countless Indian forefathers too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Yet, at the same time, they also grew their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: They established schools, temples, mosques, churches and community organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: All these have stood the test of time till today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: It is their sacrifices then, that has uplifted our generations today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In recent times, new Indian immigrants have come to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Many of them have come here to study or work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As days went, they did not return home and made Singapore their permanent home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Their aspirations are similar to our pioneers – good family, sufficient income and commitment to the country.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We are Tamils, Punjabis, Gujaratis, Malayalees, Telugus, Sindhis and many others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: And this is why I stand here today, not only as a representative of the Indian community, but as a part of the Singapore community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Our community’s progress is not apart from the country’s progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: That is what Mr S Rajaratnam, who brought glory to the Indian community and the country, emphasised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: He has said, any one community should not preserve its own traditions alone, but create a united Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: These words are especially important, given how the world is divided by language, race and religion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Singapore’s’ strength lies in the unity that we find amidst our differences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: For this unity, every community must make its contributions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: When our youths excel in education, when our seniors are fine, when our families are prosperous – this is not just a community’s achievement; it is Singapore’s victory.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As I embark my journey in this House, I hold the stories of our forefathers, the hopes of Singaporeans and new immigrants and the words of leaders such as Mr Rajaratnam in my heart.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Let us continue to build a strong and prosperous society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: May excellent Singapore excel onward. : Mr Speaker, we live in uncertain and fractious times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We face a shifting global order, the real impact of climate change and the lingering aftershocks of a once-in-a-generation pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The world today feels more volatile, polarised and far more anxious than before.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We are facing profound challenges within Singapore too – a rapidly ageing society, the rise in technology, potentially displacing jobs and greater individualism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We are also not immune to the global trends and impact of rising populism and protectionism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: However, this is not the first time Singapore had seen trouble.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Our founding generation faced severe, existential concerns, yet both the Government and people worked together to defy all odds and transform Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: My generation was born after the trauma of Separation, but we had our challenges too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: While there was palpable economic growth, there were uncertainties, economic crises and we did not take anything for granted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Like many families then, my brother and I were taught to treasure what little we had and to always care for those who needed help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This had been the ethos of the Singapore story.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: When the COVID-19 pandemic hit, I saw first-hand how the leadership worked hand in hand with our people to save lives and livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I consider it an honour to have served Singapore during the pandemic and to have the voice of the underprivileged be represented as I served, solved problems and pushed boundaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Today's generation faces different challenges and a different lived experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In fact, in my conversations with young Singaporeans, I hear both optimism and unease.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: They believe in Singapore, but they want their voices to be heard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: And they want to know that this country will work for them even as the world changes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This will therefore be my first area of focus: our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Understandably, their points of reference are different from ours, where development exists, systems work but there are expectations for them to work better.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: While there are more opportunities both locally and overseas, our youths are apprehensive about their type of jobs, their families, their future and about global justice, climate change and the environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: My colleagues and I are committed to listening to you to understand your concerns and to work with you to fulfil your dreams".

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This generation understands different pathways to success and has what it takes to overcome the hurdles that life throws at them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: While performing for the SAF military band during his National Service, he suffered a nerve injury.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: During his recovery, he discovered his talent in being a composer and a conductor.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: After receiving the Lee Kuan Yew scholarship and scoring the first prize at the Gustav Mahler Conducting Competition, Kah Chun had many notable appearances such as being appointed as chief conductor to Germany's Nuremberg Symphony Orchestra and the Japan Philharmonic Orchestra.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Last year, he was appointed the principal conductor and artistic adviser of The Hallee, a 165-year-old symphony orchestra based in Manchester in the United Kingdom.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This year, he made history as the first Singaporean to conduct at the BBC Promenade Concerts, the world famous classical music festival held annually in London.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Kah Chun had blazed the trail and had shown young Singaporeans that it is possible to carve out meaningful careers even in less conventional fields.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: To this, I would say, "Do not despair.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: My colleagues and I at MOM will do whatever we can to help to be a bridge for you and to help to connect you to jobs, assess your career health, highlight industries that are growing and to help you acquire the skills needed for roles in these sectors".

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Further, in my capacity as the co-chair of the Economic Strategy Review Committee on Entrepreneurship, I hope to be able to provide new opportunities to help fulfil your aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: My fellow co-chair Minister of State Alvin Tan and I are determined to create a bustling culture of entrepreneurship where our youths would be able to fulfil personal aspirations and in the process, solidify Singapore's place as an entrepreneurship hub.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This is another clear reflection of how the Government works with all Singaporeans to provide for better, more prosperous futures by connecting them to jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: While we secure the futures of our young, we must continue to value and respect those who had built Singapore, past and present.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This brings me to my second area of focus: our seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Singapore has been designated as a Blue Zone 2.0 country as our residents have exceptionally long life expectancies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In fact, in my constituency in Bedok and Siglap, one in four residents are already above the age of 65.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: If I were to expand the age bracket to those who are above 60, 32% or almost one third of my residents would qualify.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Many of our seniors are fit and active and have much to contribute to our nation, including our workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We should provide as many opportunities as possible, especially for those who are willing and able to work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The Ministry of Health's (MOH's) Healthier SG and Age Well SG have been significant programmes that have the potential to change the ageing landscape in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: With the speed and comprehensive nature of the rollout of both initiatives, particularly Age Well SG, residents of HDB towns would benefit tremendously from such programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Given the sheer number of seniors among us, it would be useful to expand the programme, which includes social gatherings, exercise and therapy sessions, to include private estates as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Unfortunately, not all of us will be able to age gracefully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Some of us might unfortunately be affected by illnesses and disease.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This might be so despite our best efforts in taking care of ourselves and living wisely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Suffering from a severe mental illness for many years, I could see the psychological toll it took on her entire family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Nevertheless, my in-laws took it in their stride and did their duty, always with a warm, loving smile until her last days.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I believe more can be done to support our seniors like my wife's grandmother and their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I wish to continue to push for initiatives both at the policy and implementation levels and to be a voice for our seniors to live dignified lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: My third area of focus will be on protecting the vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: One of our key policy pillars had been that families and society formed the basic safety nets for individuals with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: However, with competing demands, reducing family sizes and Singapore's economic development, it is not unreasonable for there to be an expectation for the state to do slightly more – not for the Government to be the sole safety net but to play a stronger role.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: For those who may be able to work, we should be giving them a fair wage for their efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: MOM had been rolling out the Progressive Wage Model (PWM).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: To complement the Government's efforts, businesses must also continue to restructure themselves and workers must acquire new skills to remain employable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We must not forget our migrant workers, who take on much of the toil that Singaporeans prefer not to do.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Our buildings and infrastructure are built on their blood, sweat and tears.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As if their daily contributions are not enough, they occasionally transform into superheroes to save Singaporeans in need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In my capacity at MOM, I have had the pleasure of working closely with our migrant workers and hope that Singaporeans will continue to open their hearts to them and to support them, not only when they perform heroic acts from time to time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Speaking of daily superheroes, the demands on caregivers, particularly those taking care of physically or intellectually disabled people, can be time consuming and both emotionally and financially draining.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Ultimately, Singaporeans facing physical or mental disabilities together with their families deserve to live fulfilling lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I will do my best to ensure that no one is left behind.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The uncertainties in the world are likely to continue.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: There could be pressures on our resolve and unity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Some may draw comparisons between the haves and the have-nots.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Others may turn nativist, trying to draw the distinction between second- or third-generation with first-generation Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: During such times, we should strengthen our resolve and fall back on our values.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We have always celebrated ground up initiatives based on self reliance and a strong work ethic, just like my in-laws.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Hence, wanting to be a "we first" society does not mean that we were wholly individualistic previously.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I agree with Mr President that our nation’s success must never be measured by economic growth alone.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It must be judged by how we support the vulnerable and how we enable every Singaporean to contribute and to live with dignity.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As we begin the 15th Parliament, it is timely to reflect on how far we have come in uplifting our lower-wage workers, and more importantly, the work that still lies ahead.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Over the last decade, we have made significant strides in improving the wages, welfare and work conditions of our lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This shows that our policies are lifting those at the lower end of the wage ladder.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Some ask why Singapore has not adopted a universal minimum wage.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The answer lies in the strength of our PWM.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Unlike a single wage floor applied across the board, PWM is tailored to specific sectors, covers over 40 job roles today and enables workers to progress through skills and productivity.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: A decade ago, a general office cleaner earned about $600.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Workers like Azizah Abdul Majeed, a single mother who upgraded herself from part-time cleaner to team leader, show how PWM creates dignity, career progression and better livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In the security sector, the basic monthly wage of an entry-level security officer was about $1,100 in 2016.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Many security officers are now running digital systems and handling crowd-control duties – roles now seen as skilled professions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Just as important are the personal stories behind these numbers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: One example is Sivamani Taigrajan, whose father once worked long hours as a security guard to support the family.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Today, as a Security Supervisor, she leads a command centre, embraces new technology and inspires others to join the industry.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: More than higher pay, she now has pride and purpose in a profession that has been transformed by PWM.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Gini coefficient has fallen from 0.464 in 2014 to 0.435 in 2024.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: If we take into account both transfers and taxes, the Gini coefficient drops further to 0.364.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: They were built on strong tripartite trust and tough negotiations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In 2021, the Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers put forth 18 recommendations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I am glad to know that by working together, by July 2023, all 18 recommendations were implemented.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Each year, the National Wages Council, another tripartite platform, continues to issue guidelines with a strong focus on uplifting our lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While progress has been made, the journey is far from complete.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: NTUC’s June 2025 Survey showed that lower-income households are most worried about the rising costs of food, groceries and healthcare.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Many are also supporting both young children and elderly parents.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Workers know upskilling is key but often struggle to identify relevant training or meaningful career opportunities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I had spoken about this before, in this house, highlighting the two common questions that workers have: train what?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In security, officers still work 12-hour shifts, six days a week.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Higher wages cannot come at the expense of health, well-being and family life.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Younger Singaporeans are not joining PWM sectors in sufficient numbers, raising concerns about long-term sustainability for the service providers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: PWM wage negotiations are becoming tougher in today’s economic climate and close monitoring is needed to prevent uneven application or cost-shifting.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: These challenges make it even more critical that our tripartite partners stand firm in upholding fair and sustainable outcomes for our workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Amidst these challenges, NTUC and our unions will continue to work hard to ensure that wages keep pace and workers are not left behind.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond wages, our unions play a hands-on role: negotiating fairer workplace conditions, supporting upskilling and providing aid through our NTUC U Care Fund for members and their families facing financial stress.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Income at the 20th percentile is about 55% of median income – short of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) benchmark of two-thirds.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This group must be bold, ambitious, and focused on both wages and sustained career progression.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: NTUC will also seek to broaden and deepen the impact of the PWM in two key areas.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: First, by placing stronger emphasis on productivity as the enabler of sustainable wage growth.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For example, 800 Super Waste Management, they work with the Built Environment and Urban Trades Employees’ Union (BATU), deployed AI-enabled recycling bins under a Company Training Committee framework.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This boosted productivity, reduced contamination and more importantly, enabled higher-value jobs with a 5% pay increase for 100 workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: One area that I have raised before is Pest Management, an essential service in public health but still plagued by low wages and high attrition.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: A PWM here would create structured career and wage ladders, strengthening both livelihoods and the resilience of the sector.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond PWM, the Local Qualifying Salary (LQS) ensures that firms hiring foreign manpower also uplift local wages.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The last increase brought the threshold to $1,600 in July 2024.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: At the same time, NTUC recognises that some workers may need more help.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Through the NTUC U Care Fund, we will continue to support vulnerable families and those hit by sudden hardship.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The FairPrice Group, for example, continues to keep essentials affordable, helping families cope even as wages rise.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Labour Movement has, and will continue to, do our part in helping to nurture a "we first" society at every level.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: (In Mandarin):   Over the past decade, the PWM has become an important cornerstone of our tripartite cooperation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We can see that income inequality in our country has narrowed, which proves that our policies to raise the wages of low-income workers are indeed effective.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Behind these numbers are the real workers and families: the cleaning uncle supporting his family's needs, the security officer spending more time with his family or the pest management worker seeking career development and recognition.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: NTUC will continue to walk the journey with low wage workers, working hand-in-hand with the Government, employers and the wider community to build a fairer and more inclusive Singapore.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For the new term of this Government, I urge the Government to continue pressing forward boldly.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Only in this way can we further narrow the income gap, drive sustained wage growth and enable every worker to progress with dignity. : Sir, over the past decade, PWM has become a cornerstone of our labour compact.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: More importantly, behind these numbers are real workers and real families: the cleaner supporting his children’s education, the security officer spending more time with his family, or the pest management worker seeking career recognition.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: NTUC remains firmly committed to walking this journey with our workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Together with our tripartite partners and the wider community, we will continue to build a fairer, more inclusive Singapore, where no worker is left behind.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Our citizens do not only care for their self-interest.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: I am sure the House is familiar with the term "gotong royong".

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: I want to recount the words of Han Suyin from her autobiography "My House Has Two Doors", where she described the collective founding of Nantah.
She wrote, "How many oyster omelettes, sliced crab, noodles of all kinds went into Nanyang University?

The trishaw pedallers of Singapore and Malaya pedaled for three days and turned it all in for Nanyang University, and theirs was the greatest sacrifice, for they were so very poor." She goes on to say, "Rubber tappers flocked to give; they know that their children would never have a chance to go to university, but it was a gesture of cultural identity.
It was incredible and magnificent, and it must be remembered." More importantly, our sense of generosity and solidarity extends cross-communally.
Singaporeans do care about others and we are able to see beyond our own personal interests.
In fact, our success in nation-building is a testament to our citizens working together for the public well-being.
The first relates to the unintended consequences of meritocracy.
The second is the growing sense of precariousness that many Singaporeans feel.

(In Malay): Our emphasis on meritocracy is meant to ensure that talent is appropriately rewarded and to encourage social mobility on the basis of achievement, rather than affiliation, and capability, rather than connection.
Meritocracy, when taken to an extreme, can promote the wrong impression: that those who succeed mistakenly believe that their success was achieved solely because they worked hard.
Meanwhile, those who are left behind are assumed to deserve being left behind because they have not worked hard enough.
This demonstrates how meritocracy can be turned into an "ideology", as described by Syed Hussein Alatas in his book "The Myth of the Lazy Native".
As an ideology, meritocracy is not just a mechanism to identify and sort talent, but it also becomes a belief to justify and explain away inequality and the lot of those left behind.
Such a belief can be corrosive to a "we first" society because it suggests that those who are struggling deserve to be struggling.
It creates the impression that the poor and the disadvantaged should suffer what they must since they are not hardworking enough, or not smart enough, or not capable enough.
It is also difficult to foster a "we first" society when the ethos of meritocracy tends to contribute to a narrative of "winners" and "losers".
When we find ourselves always trying to stay ahead and avoid losing out, it is not surprising that we become more concerned about personal achievement rather than the common good.
This brings me to my point about precariousness.
Many Singaporeans live with a sense of precariousness.
This is especially acute among the lower-income segments of the population.
Many are feeling squeezed by the rising costs of living.
Meanwhile, our local entrepreneurs also find themselves increasingly priced out by rental hikes.

They feel as though their lives are precarious, their futures and their children's futures are deeply uncertain, and they worry that everything they have worked hard for could be lost with just one unfortunate mistake or accident. : Mr Speaker, I just explained that when we uncritically idealise meritocracy, we risk blaming the disadvantaged for their plight and lauding the successful for their fortune.
We cripple our own willingness to aid those who live paycheck to paycheck, those who are, today, condemned to an increasingly precarious existence.
I make the point about precariousness to highlight how difficult it is to think about the "we", when the "me" is valiantly struggling to make ends meet and eke out a living.
The House should not just exhort our citizens to do more, but also call on the Government to take the lead in ensuring that all Singaporeans can pursue a dignified life.
Moreover, I believe that when each and every person is afforded with dignity, it can lead to a more civic and public-minded behaviour.
It means that no matter their background and no matter their lot in life, every Singaporean must be able to contribute to society and receive support from society.
Importantly, this means that those who are falling behind or may need additional help are regarded with respect and their needs properly accommodated, instead of being treated as a burden on others.
On this occasion, Sir, I want to focus on dignity as it relates to our elderly.
It is unconscionable that some of them remain classed among the working poor, having to make a living through menial jobs, even in their 60s and 70s.

Every Member of this House would have met the cleaners, delivery workers and hawker stall assistants in their constituencies who are forced to persist in gruelling labour, despite their advanced age and sometimes, in spite of health issues.
Some of them might even find themselves having to live in rental homes with other strangers.
Even as I admire their resilience and work ethic, I am sure that we can do better for our elderly.
This House would surely agree that being forced into this situation is not a dignified way of living out one's golden years.
We all want the best for our elderly.
More importantly, we do not resent or begrudge them as they develop more needs as they grow older.
Rather, we recognise that it is a matter of their dignity that we do our best to accommodate those needs.
However, a "we first" society, especially one as wealthy as ours, must also attend to our elderly's post-material needs to enable them to pursue a life of dignity.
To live your golden years, with peace of mind in a quiet place that you can call your own, without having to worry about your next meal, medical bill or bus ride.
Such a life of dignity is surely what we owe to our Pioneer and Merdeka generations after they have devoted their prime years to Singapore.

To me, however, the more pertinent question is: what can we do to make it easier for our senior citizens to live a dignified life, to feel respected and secure as our fellow citizens and recognise that they do belong to Singapore, as independent and autonomous persons rather than a social burden?

In facilitating their mobility, the elderly not only retain their independence and autonomy, but it can also encourage their participation in social activities and allow them to continue being an active member of society.
And I am sure that most, if not all, Singaporeans would not begrudge offering such dignity to the elderly.
A "we first" society must be sensitive to the different needs of different groups, which includes being prepared to offer an extra helping hand if the situation requires it.
Aimé Césaire once poetically described how "there is a place for all at the Rendezvous of Victory".
This, however, requires the Government to sometimes step in, so that each and every Singaporean has the opportunity to lead a life with dignity.

This creates a virtuous circle, when all of us are assured the opportunity to pursue a life of dignity, it comes naturally to us to be more attentive and extend our consideration to those who are disadvantaged or not as fortunate.
As I have stated at the outset, Singaporeans are not selfish people.
We care for others and we follow that up with concrete actions.
History has shown that we are able to set aside our personal interests and, sometimes, even sacrifice them for a common cause.
These sentiments of collective solidarity, however, cannot simply be forced.
But they can be nurtured by ensuring that all citizens have the resources and opportunities needed to pursue a dignified life.
This would foster the sense of security and belonging necessary to motivate collective action.
In other words, it is only when each one of us feels that we are truly valued members of society that we can become a "we first" society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Earlier, Deputy Prime Minister Gan and Members of the House spoke about geopolitical tension, economic volatility, technological disruption and the looming crisis of climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, I will focus on one of the greatest threats to our generation, that is, climate disruption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And around the world, the pace of climate action is slowing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In fact, some countries have already wavered in their Paris Agreement pledges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Even with current commitments, the world is on track for warming of two to three degrees, well beyond the 1.5 degrees that science tells us is safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But we will still feel the full force of climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While we cannot change the world's trajectory alone, we must be prepared to live with its consequences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said in his National Day Rally speech, "We must look ahead, anticipate what is on the horizon and prepare to ride the next wave of change." That is the hallmark of the PAP government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We govern not just for the next election cycle, but for the future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Throughout our history, the PAP government has made bold decisions with foresight and discipline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We invested in water resilience before others even thought about it – NEWater, desalination, local catchments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We transformed waste management with incineration and adapted Pulau Semakau.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We cleaned up the Singapore River and tackled air pollution long before environmentalism was fashionable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As our founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew once declared: "I am calculating not in terms of the next election, I am calculating in terms of the next generation; in terms of the next 100 years; in terms of eternity." This was said back in 1965 and this spirit endures in today's political leadership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singapore's future and our survival is at the front and centre of everything that we do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is backed by long-term thinking across generations of leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is not an elections or political slogan.
