speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are just four or five months out into the new term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But it is a serious financial commitment, one that we planned prudently and that we will fund sustainably through our fiscal policies and reserves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There are very, very few countries in the world that can say the same.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Think about East Coast Park, Sentosa, Eunos-Kembangan and possibly up to Tanjong Katong, under water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Imagine Singapore without the coastlines that we are familiar with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: No evening jogs or family picnics at East Coast Park.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These could be just memories of what we used to be, if we did nothing today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over the years, the Government has spent billions of dollars on our canals and drains to prevent floods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But extreme rainfall will only mean that flash floods in urban areas will only get more common if we do not act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The question is whether we can overcome practical constraints to engineering and costs to cater to extreme weather, given our tight landmass and highly developed urban areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year was the hottest year on record globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And in Singapore, our coldest month today is already warmer than our warmest month in the 1960s – imagine that.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We import more than 90% of our food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Floods, droughts and export bans can disrupt supplies overnight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We saw this during COVID and got us thinking of new approaches and strategies to develop food resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our Four National Taps give us resilience but the changing weather patterns and rising demand means that we must work harder.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These are not distant scenarios, ladies and gentlemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They are today's lived reality and we can already feel the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At first glance, climate adaptation feels like setting up various defence measures across the country – sea walls, drains, polder systems, solar panels and food stockpiles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: History shows us why such long-term projects matter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When Marina Barrage was first proposed, there were many who doubted its feasibility and value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, it is one of Singapore's most iconic landmarks – a reservoir, a flood barrier, a place where families gather for recreation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: What was once a bold idea has now become a national treasure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While it was built for flood control and water supply, it is now a place where families picnic, students learn, and communities gather.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: That is the approach that we must take, protecting our people and our assets with a purpose, and creating greater value in adaptation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are embarking on a generational effort to protect our coastlines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The "Long Island" project along East Coast Park will be more than just a seawall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It will include reclaimed land for homes, a freshwater reservoir and new spaces for recreation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are creating value for our people by providing more homes, more facilities and more opportunities, while protecting our coastline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At Pulau Tekong, we have completed Singapore’s first polder.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The polder used half the sand required of conventional reclamation, while increasing the training space for the SAF – the size of two Toa Payoh towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have launched site-specific studies for Greater Southern Waterfront, Changi, Jurong Island and more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Piece by piece, we are creating a ring of resilience around Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But we are not on this journey alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The PAP government will continue to build trust with Singaporeans and bring our people with us for this journey and for the long haul.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also consult nature groups like the Nature Society because resilience must also mean shared ownership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As President Tharman reminded us in his President’s Address that, "This trust has allowed us to make hard choices when needed and to plan for the future beyond current election cycles".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is precisely what adaptation demands: choices need to be made today, for risks that may arise decades ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These measures will enhance the flood resilience of their premises, while allowing solutions that best integrate with the design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are also working with businesses and residents in flood-prone areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: No matter how strong the storms are ahead, the Government will work with you to overcome them together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I will now share our plans for heat resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It covers urban planning, building design, public health and community awareness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government has a national heatwave response plan to protect Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this will require the collective effort of the Government, our employers, and our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For workers involved in heavy physical labour, employers will keep a close watch on heat stress levels and ensure that they have sufficient hydration and rest, away from the sun.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Students can dress down or switch to home-based learning if needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Besides the efforts from the Government, the public can also play its part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Volunteers can check on vulnerable groups, such as the elderly in our community, to ensure that they are adequately protected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We can open cooling centres at Community Clubs (CCs) and the Resident's Committees (RCs) for vulnerable groups and monitor patients and seniors in hospitals and eldercare centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through the myENV app, the public can also get timely Heat Stress Advisory information on how to protect themselves according to heat stress levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But ultimately, resilience is not just about infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Just as Total Defence reminds us that every Singaporean has a role in our security, climate defence requires collective action by everyone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And the test will come during an extreme climate event.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Will we stand together, support the vulnerable and act as one people?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: That is what will define us as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are also learning from others who face extreme heat today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are studying heatwaves in Europe, heat adaptation measures in the Middle East and exploring novel cooling methods with researchers and preparing before such extreme events reach our shores.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Looking ahead, we are strengthening whole-of-Government coordination and partnering businesses, academia and the community, to develop an integrated Heat Resilience Strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will create shaded walkways, green corridors and cooling zones, which will improve liveability while making our neighbourhoods healthier and more walkable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Already, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA), and the Housing and Development Board (HDB) are testing and scaling innovative measures like new wind flow modelling technologies and cooling materials in our estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These are among new innovations that can potentially make a difference in our daily comfort in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Food is part of our culture and our identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, floods, droughts and heatwaves are affecting crops globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: COVID-19 was a stark reminder of our vulnerabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I recall in 2020, there were concerns that countries' COVID-19 measures would lead to food supply disruptions, such as eggs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this led to increased demand for eggs overnight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Yet, within days, we were able to reassure the public of continued supply due to our diversified sources and stabilised demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: That is why we are diversifying our sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Before COVID, eggs came mostly from one country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Even as we increase local food production, we will work to facilitate food imports from new sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the industry level, we will support our local importers to nurture strong relationships with business partners through overseas sourcing and business matching trips.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our local farms and food production still matter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And we are helping our farms to scale by addressing key challenges of productivity, cost and demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want to encourage local farms to tap on technology to grow food in a more productive and climate-resilient manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through the Agri-Food Cluster Transformation (ACT) Fund, farms, such as Green Harvest, have invested in a hydroponics greenhouse with automated mobile gulley system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This has made them five times more productive than traditional farms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When we support our local farmers and buy more local produce, such as chye sim or seabass, we are building resilience for ourselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When Singaporeans choose produce with the SG Fresh Produce branding at supermarkets or wet markets, you are directly supporting our farmers and our food security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Local produce is fresher, lasts longer, incurs lower carbon footprint to reach us and many are pesticide-free.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am glad that industry players, through SAFEF (Singapore Agro-Food Enterprises Federation Limited), are already working on long-term contracts between farmers and buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For Singapore, water is a precious and limited resource.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As then-Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said in 2021: "Water is a strategic and scarce resource, and also a precious fruit of our labours...We are always pushing the limits of our water resources." We have over successive decades built a robust and diversified water supply, made possible by right-pricing water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have built up our Four National Taps – local catchment, imported water, NEWater and desalination – to strengthen our water resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But as our population and economy grows, and as weather patterns change, we have to work harder to conserve this precious resource because water security is also national security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singapore's waste system is so efficient to the point that it is pretty much out of sight, out of mind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As Singapore becomes more affluent and develops new industries, we will produce and consume more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Hence, if we do not manage our waste well, we will face issues of disposing them within the next just 10 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For food waste, large commercial and industrial food waste generators in new buildings, they must now segregate food waste for treatment, and this will be extended to more and more buildings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The AfA on Packaging Waste Reduction for the E-Commerce Sector, which included players like Amazon and Shopee, has developed guidelines to encourage the use of sustainable packaging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In our estates, new initiatives, such as REhub bins allow residents to deposit recyclables, scan QR codes and track recycling habits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This helps to build awareness and give families a sense of ownership in reducing waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But we must also recognise that we have room to improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our overall recycling rate stands at about 50%, as compared to 63% in Australia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This comparison is a reminder that Singapore can and must do better with our collective effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Everyone can do the 3Rs – reduce consumption, reuse what you can, recycle right.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this only works if we all commit, together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Despite the backsliding of global climate action, Singapore must stay the course in our transition to a low carbon future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There is the economic imperative to ensure that our businesses and jobs remain competitive for the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to support businesses with incentives to improve their energy efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Based on the latest data from the International Energy Agency, Singapore's energy intensity would rank amongst the lowest one-third, if compared to all OECD countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singapore imports almost all of our energy supply and it is important that Singapore raises our energy efficiency to make every joule count.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As businesses improve on their energy efficiency, we will continue to calibrate the price signal through the carbon tax, which aims to enhance the business case for low-carbon solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government uses the carbon tax we collect to support businesses in the green transition and we encourage adoption of low-carbon technologies, such as solar power.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are also partnering industry for other climate mitigation measures, such as high-quality carbon credits, as well as cross-border carbon capture and storage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As regional countries explore nuclear power, we are building capabilities in nuclear science and safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute, we aim to grow from 50 to 100 experts by 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this will allow us to assess risks prudently, and plan for long-term possibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Climate Friendly Households Programme supports households in switching to efficient appliances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This helps households save on utility bills, while helping to lower our carbon footprint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are also making full use of our land.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: By 2030, nearly every HDB block with a suitable rooftop will be fitted with solar panels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These panels power common services – lifts, lights, and water pumps – directly lowering energy costs for residents and Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Every adaptation measure I have shared – whether it is $100 billion in coastal protection, national heat strategies, food and water resilience, or circular economy innovation – reflects more than just engineering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It reflects a philosophy of governance, a philosophy rooted in the PAP government's long-term view, passed down from our founding fathers, across generations of political leaders and to the 4G leaders of today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is rooted in fiscal prudence, political will and the conviction that every generation must leave behind a stronger foundation for the next.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The NAP will be our living roadmap to address the physical risks and social impact of climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is the commitment that my colleagues and I at the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) bring to this work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We plan, we prepare, and we act early, because safeguarding Singapore is our first duty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: President Tharman shared in his address at the Opening of this Session Parliament, "We will nurture a 'we first' society at every level, starting in the community." That is our calling today, to take the long view, to put "we before me", to protect tomorrow with resilience, steward today's resources responsibly and ensure that Singapore, our little red dot, continues to thrive in a turbulent world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is the PAP government's promise, to govern not just for the next election, but for future generations to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And for us, for all of us here in this Chamber, to do so with the same courage and foresight of our founding fathers, that built the Singapore that we enjoy today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In Malay): Mr Speaker, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong stated in his National Day Speech that, "We must also look ahead – anticipate what is on the horizon, and prepare to ride the next wave of change." Climate change is the greatest challenge of our generation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is not a future issue – it is already happening.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Heat is increasing, rainfall is getting heavier and sea levels are rising.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singapore only contributes 0.1% of global emissions, but we will feel its full impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Here lies the uniqueness of the PAP government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: From the beginning, we have never governed just for electoral cycles, but for the future of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As demonstrated by Mr Lee Kuan Yew in the Singapore Water Story, the Government does not shy away from tough decisions, plan for decades ahead and ensure that we allocate resources to carry out the plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This spirit has enabled Singapore to survive, and this same spirit also guides us in facing climate change today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The polder at Pulau Tekong demonstrates that we can protect our coastline in a more resource-efficient manner, whilst giving the SAF a larger training space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: During heat waves, we can issue warnings through the myENV application, as well as protect workers and students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But resilience is not just about infrastructure – it is about society's attitude to stand together, just like the spirit of Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: During COVID-19, we saw how supplies can be easily affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Now, we import eggs from over 10 countries and our local farms increased their production through modern technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also encourage citizens to buy local products with the SG Fresh Produce label.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said in 2021, water is a strategic resource and our most precious energy product – that is why the PAP government continues to invest with fiscal discipline and foresight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If nothing is done, Semakau Island will be completely filled by 2035.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is how the PAP government works – we do not run away from trade-offs or challenging issues, but plan boldly with a view for the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singapore has achieved the 2025 solar target much earlier, and by 2023 almost all suitable HDB rooftops will have solar panels installed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also import renewable energy through the LTMS project, while supporting households with Climate Vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: All of this shows that we are not only resilient, but also remain competitive in the future green economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But it is also an opportunity to show what makes Singapore different – we have a Government that boldly plans decades ahead, has fiscal discipline, and is committed to taking care of the people beyond electoral cycles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As President Tharman underlined in the President’s address "We will nurture a "we first" society at every level." For me and my colleagues MSE, this is our commitment – to plan ahead, protect our people, and ensure Singapore is always prepared to face climate challenges.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Fadli, I will give you some time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will call on Ms Tin Pei Ling first.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: President, in his speech, spoke of Singapore being at a critical juncture in our history as we celebrate SG60, and the importance of how we must remain resilient and inclusive, embracing the "we first" mindset, even as we navigate a turbulent world and transform for the future.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Indeed, Singapore's story has been remarkable, characterised by a silent defiance.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: When Singapore became independent in 1965, many doubted our survival.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We were a small nation with no natural resources.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Deep social divides, racial riots and hostile neighbours could have torn us apart.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Through grit, unity and foresight, we transformed ourselves into a thriving economy and a cohesive society that we are proud of today.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Our early generations refused to be defined by limitations and built a nation greater than the sum of its parts.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Then, defying the odds of de-globalisation and a turbulent world.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Today, the odds we face are different, but just as formidable.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: The global order is shifting, major powers are contesting influence and the economic climate is more uncertain than ever.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Following the Cold War, Pax Americana shaped the international order, building institutions, establishing rules-based international order and delivering a long period of relative stability and prosperity.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: If a single hegemon ceases to act as a steady, rules‑based steward, the global system can be destabilised.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Recent trends, from abrupt policy shifts, perceived abandonment of allies, sudden tariff escalations and weakening of multilateral and international bodies have exposed those vulnerabilities and heightened geopolitical uncertainty.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: These have significant impact on how supply chains are structured, on trade and talent flows and definitely on Singapore.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Interestingly, in a recent closed door sharing organised by my firm with large scale international payment service providers supporting cross border trade, an observation made was that trade is now more point-to-point, as opposed to passing through central nodes.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Also, "friendshoring" by firms would also mean that trades happen within allied blocs.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Singapore would have to ensure that we continue to participate in the various trading blocs, which we have been thankfully so far.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: But this is also contingent on not being forced to choose sides.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: As countries increasingly turn inward, doubting the benefits of globalisation and retreating from multilateralism, one wonders how Singapore companies can still dream global?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Hence, in the face of these extrinsic challenges, Singapore must remain a stable node in an unstable world.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: A place where investors can trust the rule of law, where talent knows merit is valued and where citizens feel secure amidst global disruption.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: At the same time, we must be a stable node that is resilient.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: As a hub, we have to offer secure and diversified services to support the supply chains and trade.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We also have to enhance our trade facilitation and digital services to keep competitive.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We must also be a stable node with many connections.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We must continue to be among the world's most open and connected hubs, in air and sea transport, in trade and finance, in talent, data flows and digital networks.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Here, I applaud our Government's efforts in constantly building up our position as air and sea hubs.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It is also encouraging to know of our Government's efforts to sign more Free Trade Agreements and Digital Economy Agreements, making sure we maintain high standards and inter-operability for data, digital infrastructure and networks so that trade and innovation can still flourish.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Technological advancements have been enablers but also game changers.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Singapore may not be known for inventing foundational technologies, but we can invent new systems and excel in applications built upon these technologies.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: For example, leverage our strategic position in ASEAN and build regional digital financial infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It could be inter-operable payment rails using tokens to reduce our region's overreliance on any particular currency or cross border payment rail.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It could be a cross‑border real‑time payments utility hosted in Singapore, given our strong legal and regulatory trust framework.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It could be a tokenised trade and commodities platforms to facilitate trade finance.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Some of these are probably already being considered by the Government or happening as we speak.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: These are just broad ideas and examples of how Singapore can defy the odds of our extrinsic reality.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I am sure there are many other and better ideas out there.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: So, in this term, I urge that we continue promoting public-private partnerships to discover new ideas, to deliver excellence and to create new possibilities for Singapore.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Ultimately, our relentless pursuit for economic progress – survival, in this case – is and must be rooted in our pursuit of improving lives for our people.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: So, even as the world churns and pressures, Singapore must endeavour to remain stable.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: As others build walls, Singapore will build bridges.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: The way we live, work and play are different.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Our policies, approach and infrastructure have to evolve.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Gen Z today face challenges different from that of mine.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, Gen Z Singaporeans missed out on internships and overseas exchange experiences.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Also, with the rise of AI, entry-level jobs are affected and job search strategies that used to work may no longer work now.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Fragmented career paths could be a permanent trend.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It is, thus, heartening to observe the Government's efforts in supporting our youths in their education and employment.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Such efforts to empower and keep them relevant must continue.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Many may see an ageing population as a burden, but in Singapore, we can and should shape how we age.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We can organise ourselves so that seniors enjoy healthier and more fulfilling lives supported by better healthcare, stronger communities and lifelong learning.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Much has been said about how to support our seniors better, so I will not expound them again here.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: But what is worth repeating is that we must make sure that our seniors today and tomorrow do not give up on themselves.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We must not be handicapped by our own prejudices towards old age.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We must continue to work on our policies, infrastructure and programmes to enable seniors to live healthier, work better, if they so choose, and play harder.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Defy the odds by transforming longevity into our source of strength.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It is not just our people who age.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Singapore's hardware and infrastructure, from HDB flats and estate common facilities to rail networks, power cables and more, underpin daily and community life, economic activity and national resilience.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Much of this built capital has served our nation well for decades, but with demographic shifts, technological changes, climate risks and simply the passage of time, mean that the "business as usual" maintenance and periodic upgrades are no longer sufficient.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Singapore must refresh existing hardware and infrastructure more intensively and build new, future‑ready ones to sustain living standards.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Pipes, lifts, walls, ceilings and other components in flats and housing precincts suffer wear, obsolescence and greater fault frequency, worse if they happen together.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: For those of us who have mature housing estates, will know that the lifts cannot last until the recommended 28 years.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: For example, an aging population means greater use of lifts, means more sheltered walkways with more benches needed for resting along the way.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: With the move to using more electronic vehicles and eventually autonomous vehicles as well, more charging stations and other infrastructure will be needed, and so space and power allocation has to change.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Overall, planning norms, quality standards and budgets will have to change.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Thirdly, climate changes will add to the challenges we face.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Higher temperatures, more intense storms and rising sea levels can accelerate material degradation, strain our drainage and power systems and increase the need for backup and emergency response capabilities.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: A tough job for the Ministry of Finance (MOF).

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Though refreshing or building new infrastructure is not exactly defying the odds, it is important because the right build environment can free us from everyday friction, sharpen our focus, spark creativity and unlock our best performance.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: (In Mandarin): In his address at the Opening of Parliament, President Tharman pointed out that Singapore stands at a historical juncture.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Despite global turbulence and mounting uncertainties, we must maintain resilience and inclusivity, moving forward with steady steps towards the future.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: This extraordinariness stems from Singaporeans' quiet determination to "never give up." We never give up: rising from historical adversity.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Our forefathers refused to let circumstances limit us.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Through perseverance, unity and foresight, Singapore became a prosperous economy and harmonious society that makes us proud today.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We never give up: we must strive to break through amidst de-globalisition and a turbulent world.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Today, we face different but equally severe adversities.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Therefore, even as the world fluctuates with both old and new pressures coexisting, Singapore must still strive for stability.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: When other nations build walls, we must build bridges.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We must uphold the rule of law, strengthen external and domestic trust in our institutions, remain open whilst ensuring our citizens feel secure amidst turbulence.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We never give up: demographics need not be a constraint.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Population is aging; younger generation is facing vastly different challenges, lifestyles are also changing accordingly.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Our policy formulation and implementation must stay relevant.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: But in Singapore, we can and should reshape how we view old age.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Over the years, our government has been committed to supporting our elderly to live healthier, more fulfilling and more productive lives through better healthcare and more diverse social and community structures.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We must reject the negative mindset of "waiting to die" or "being useless when old." We must strive to give all Singaporeans, young and old, reasons and motivation to look forward to each new day.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: With our never-give-up spirit, we will transform longevity into a source of strength.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Just now, WP parliamentary colleagues seemed to insinuate that my party is autocratic in their speech.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Since coming to power, the PAP has consistently upheld a people-centric philosophy in governing the nation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Whilst our governing methods may differ at various points in time, our original intentions and principles remain unchanged.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: In the early days of independence, we faced harsh and volatile environment, surrounded by challenges on all sides.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: This naturally required decisive leadership to lead the people and nation through difficulties.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: On the international stage, though we are a small red dot, our voice is not small, and the overall quality of life for our people has been substantially improved.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: This could only be achieved through the dedication of our leaders and the full cooperation of our people.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Today, we have had three Prime Ministers and welcome the fourth generation of leadership led by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: In the Prime Minister’s many important speeches, he has consistently emphasised people-centric governance and a We-first sprit.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: The Prime Minister has also promised that the Government will continue to listen to Singaporeans' voices through various channels, so that we can all participate in nation-building, build trust and deepen our national identity to achieve common goals.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Facing a diverse society, we must be inclusive and accommodating, drawing strengths from all and learning from each other, so that we can go far.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: As elected MPs, we will certainly follow the same philosophy, serve wholeheartedly and trust our constituents, living up to their expectations.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: As a democratic country, of course we cannot be autocratic.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: The key point is that we do not make compromises because we fear losing.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We do so because we choose to have our nation and the people at heart and work for the long-term interests of the country and people. : Sir, this year, we celebrate SG60.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: As a Singaporean, I am glad that we have not let our forefathers down.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Singapore remains a shining red dot on the world stage.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Yet, as President Tharman reminded us, Singapore now stands again at a pivotal moment.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: A nation tested by history, by the turbulence of a shifting world and by profound domestic changes.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Singapore has always risen to respond to challenges time and again, through our openness and resilience, through our long-term planning and willingness to take action, through our resolve, grit and unity.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: And it shall be no different now as we mark SG60.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: At this point, I would also like to take the opportunity to thank the residents of MacPherson and the broader Marine Parade-Braddell Heights group representation constituency (GRC).

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We have grown together for so many years in the past.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We have overcome many different and difficult moments, including the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Together, we have come up with new ideas to strengthen our community, to better our services, to deliver common good for the broader community.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We have raised funds and crowdsourced for ideas, and I believe that we will continue to grow stronger together.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: It is really a good example of a "we first" society.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: It is a good example of a "we first" society where we can work together towards a common good.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: President Tharman Shanmugaratnam reminded us that the world is changing in profound ways; that our global order is fraying; that we must face the future with foresight, with fortitude and with faith in one another.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Allow me to frame my remarks under three themes.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: First, unity at home; second, competitiveness through innovation; and third, conviction in the rule of law.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They are the fortress where values are first planted and resilience, nurtured.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The President was right to emphasise that we must continue to support parents, children and seniors, whether through childcare, housing, eldercare, or help for blended and multi-generation families.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Five years ago in my maiden Parliamentary speech in this House, I spoke about my son’s love of playing with Lego blocks and how each Lego brick is like our family unit; the building blocks of our society, with each one unique in shape and form and how we can enhance support and connection with one another.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I have taught my son to pick up chess.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What began as a game, quickly became a way for me to share life lessons.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: First, the goal is to capture the king; you can risk everything, but not your queen.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Second, if you play to avoid losing a single piece, then you will surely play to lose.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Third, whether you are king or pawn, everyone returns to the same wooden box in the end.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These, Mr Speaker, are not just lessons in chess, but also lessons in love and in life.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We protect what is most precious to us, we take bold steps when needed and in the end, we must remember that what matters is not status, but how we played the game, the game of life.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Beyond families and into our communities, racial and religious harmony, meritocracy, also form the vital glue that holds a nation together through times of change.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In our pursuit of growth and progress, these must never be sacrificed or compromised, for they are not negotiable assets but enduring safeguards of our collective well-being.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Lesson number one: just as in chess, where the goal must be to capture the king but one must never recklessly risk the queen, we must strive for success and advancement, yet we must never endanger the sanctity of family life and our racial and religious harmony.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Beyond this, let us strengthen parental support, expand inter-generational programmes, enhance after-school care and provide more relief for caregivers.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Just as in chess, every piece matters, in Singapore every family, no matter its form, deserves our support.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our nation’s story is one of sacrifice and solidarity.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must continue to choose "we first", not "me first".

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must adapt faster, innovate bolder, compete on skill, on speed and on trust.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Here, too, the lessons of chess offer some wisdom.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Lesson number two: if you play only to avoid losing a single piece, then you will surely play to lose.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The player who hesitates, clinging to pieces, fearing change, will soon find himself cornered.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The master anticipates, innovates and deploys each piece to the best advantage.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Likewise, if Singapore clings to old ways, paralysed by fear of change, we will be overtaken.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To win, we must anticipate, take calculated risks and deploy every piece to its best advantage.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Enterprises that harness artificial intelligence, green technologies and advanced manufacturing are like bishops and rooks, powerful when used with foresight.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But innovation must not stop with businesses or workers.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If we remain restless in innovation, relentless in improvement and responsible in governance, then like a skilful chess player, we will not merely react to the board but we can be five moves ahead.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We will shape the game and remain resilient in a shifting world.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Tariff wars and protectionism are weakening global trade rules.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In conflict zones and humanitarian crisis places, like Gaza, civilians suffer most when international humanitarian law is disregarded.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Here too, I return to that simple lesson I shared with my son.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Lesson number three: at the end of the game, whether you are king or pawn, everyone goes back into the same wooden box.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is a reminder of humility, of equality and of the limits of power.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In chess, even the strongest piece must obey the rules, without them, the game collapses into chaos.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Likewise, in international relations, rules and law are what protect the small from the strong, the weak from the powerful.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For Singapore, this means upholding fairness and the rule of law at home, ensuring justice is impartial, combating foreign interference, protecting our people from crime and terrorism.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Internationally, it means standing up for the rules-based order, defending open trade against protectionism, affirming humanitarian principles that shield civilians from suffering.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore may be small, but when we stand by principle, we are larger than our size.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In choosing rules over power, we safeguard not only ourselves but the very system that allows small states, like us, to stand tall.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore's position on the international stage is not merely due to the extent of our territory or economic strength, but because we firmly uphold international law, principles of justice, and the resolve to always become a trustworthy partner nation.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, although we are small on the world map, we wield considerable voice and influence, because we stand tall on a foundation of principles.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Even as the world outside is increasingly in turmoil, marked by division and conflict, Singapore must not waver.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Racial and religious harmony is our most important heritage, while social cohesion and meritocracy is our most powerful weapon.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As long as we stand together as one nation, our spirit will not waver – because in unity lies the strength of a country with a great soul.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In fact, this has been the PAP government's approach all along.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For us, meritocracy and helping those who need it more do not contradict each other.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Prof Kenneth Tan and Prof Hussein Alatas also emphasised that not everyone starts from the same position.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore's meritocracy system is not just for development alone, but to uplift everyone.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, our meritocracy in Singapore is also accompanied by compassion.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our meritocracy gives us the opportunity to help those who need it more.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is the "we first" that the President and Prime Minister Lawrence Wong meant. : Mr Speaker, Sir, the word gotong royong, since it is the Malay language one, duat gotong royong. "Gotong" is derived from the Javanese verb "ngotong", which signifies the act of carrying a burden. "Royong" implies doing it together.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Meritocracy is our shared commitment to help one another with compassion, our "gotong-royong", this is how we Singaporeans carry each other together.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Just like the chess lessons I gave to my son who is going to sit for his Primary School Leaving Examination soon, we safeguard what is dearest, we act with courage when the moment calls for it and, in the end, it is not rank that defines us, but the integrity with which we played the game.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Hence, if we keep our families firm and our society inclusive; if we keep our people skilled, our enterprises bold and our Government innovative with integrity; if we keep our politics principled and our laws respected, our people united, then like a well-played game of chess, Singapore will not just survive in this turbulent tournament of nations, but secure a stronger, fairer and more united future for generations to come.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling you have a clarification?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I begin by declaring that I work in a global investment firm with investments in defence-related companies.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In the opening chapter of the Chinese novel, "Romance of the Three Kingdoms", we find a line that carries through the ages: "天下大势，分久必合，合久必分".

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Great powers come together after a period of fracture; and divide after a period of unity.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Regions fracture, only to converge again under new banners.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The map of the world is never still.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is like the tide – advancing, retreating, flowing.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For small, open nations like ours, the world today is not only uncertain.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is like a gathering storm at an inflection point, where old certainties collapse into turbulence.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The assumptions that once held steady – open trade, safe sea lanes, shared global norms – can no longer be taken for granted.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Supertankers and fleets of all sizes are shifting course, switching lanes and creating waves.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For a small vessel like Singapore, the challenge is not to command the seas.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is to chart a careful passage through them.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This inflection point is not only geopolitical; it is economic and technological.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The next era will be built on electrification – from renewable grids to new storage systems.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Electrification is still in its early stages, but will rise sharply in the years ahead.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As Ray Dalio warns, we are entering a period of “multi-dimensional conflict” – spanning economics, technology and geopolitics.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: He notes that the United States’ (US') relative position has declined, while China’s rise has been remarkable.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Together, they form the twin pillars of our survival.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: His words remind us: this is not business as usual.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I speak today not only as the Chair of the Defence and Foreign Affairs Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC), but also as the Member of Parliament (MP) of Yio Chu Kang.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: From one vantage point, I see the shifting sands of geopolitics.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: From another, I hear the everyday anxieties of Singaporean families – about jobs, about costs, about our children’s future.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Political transitions in our neighbours bring forth opportunity and uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Globally, wars in Europe and the Middle East shake supply chains and energy security.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Great power rivalry between the US and China sharpens by the day.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Even in advanced democracies, societies fracture not with bombs or tanks, but with inequality, disinformation and digital disruption.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If foreign policy begins at home, then the lesson is clear: when nations grow divided inside, they stumble abroad.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And when they stumble, the shockwaves ripple across the world.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For Singapore, whose survival depends on stability abroad and cohesion at home, the stakes could not be higher.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Strengthening ties with existing allies is good, but we must avoid over-dependence.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must also cultivate diversified relationships, even with non-traditional partners in the Global South, for example, emerging economies that share an interest in regional stability.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: At the same time, we have to carefully manage risks from states who may not always share our worldview and whose ambition may not always align with a rules-based order.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) must not just keep pace.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But it is not enough to buy the most advanced systems.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What matters is whether we can sustain and replenish them.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A handful of elite systems may not decide the outcome.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is where our defence industry plays a role.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: ST Engineering has shown what is possible with reliability and innovation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must build on that and encourage more to innovate for the next generation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But we must also retain high-value technical talent, rather than lose them once trained.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Total Defence volunteerism is expanding, but participation alone is not enough.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must measure outcomes in terms of readiness and trust, not just headcount.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our defence industry can provide high-value jobs, strengthen technological sovereignty and be a source of national pride.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The challenge is to sustain strength, while keeping it affordable.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, our foreign policy must adapt just as quickly.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Principles are like a compass to set our long-term direction.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Deepening ties with both the US and China demands careful, calibrated messaging.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Openness to one must never be misread as turning away from the other.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When big nations clash, Singaporeans feel it – in the price of groceries, the security of jobs, the reliability of essential services.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our external relationships are directly tied to stability at home.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) remains our cornerstone.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) expands its missions in Africa and Latin America, the intent is right.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But we must ensure that resources are not overstretched.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The ability to pick up the phone, call a counterpart and have trust built over years.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In our own region, many of the old leaders have passed on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must invest in the new generation of connections.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must have people who can sit at tables, share meals and build trust beyond formalities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It requires credibility backed by defence, curiosity about the world and resilience at home.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is also about the resilience of our communities in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In my constituency Yio Chu Kang, I see how strong communities make strong nations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These may seem small compared to geopolitics, but they are not.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And solidarity is the true bedrock of resilience.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As Vice-Chair of the Health GPC, I have seen first-hand how these initiatives are not just policies on paper, but create real impact on the ground.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Preventive health, functional screenings, community fitness programmes and mental health outreach are transforming the way Singaporeans think about health.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They bring care into the neighbourhood, where people live, know each other and can support one another.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is where resilience takes root – in the neighbour who checks in, in the resident who volunteers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Yet, we must also address challenges to jobs and social mobility.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Still, most Singaporeans believe hard work can improve their circumstances.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We have looked at warfare today, from drones and cyberattacks to AI-enabled systems and the need for an SAF that is ready and resilient.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We have considered foreign policy that is principled and practical, open but credible, designed to deliver for our people.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We have seen how resilient communities, rooted in solidarity, form the foundation of national strength.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Through it all, defence, diplomacy and community must be sustainable, guided by careful planning and prudent stewardship.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Singapore is like a small vessel sailing in waters where giants move.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If we drift without care, we risk being capsized.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There are strategic dangers if great powers disengage and economic dangers if rivalries fracture supply chains.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To endure, we must see risks early, seize opportunities fast and equip our ship with radar, engines, reserves and most importantly, a disciplined and united crew.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Recently, a Yio Chu Kang family came to see me at my meet-the-people session (MPS).

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A member had faced a serious road incident abroad.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Delays in medical care, challenges with local authorities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I met them recently during my community walkabouts.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is the price of groceries, the security of jobs, the reliability of services.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The assurance that when you are in trouble abroad, your country will not leave you behind.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: So, when history looks back, in 2035, 2050 or 2065 when we celebrate SG100, let it record that we did not shrink from the challenge.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We secured our sovereignty, held fast to our unity, and built resilience across generations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is our moment to ride out the storm.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must move with confidence, clarity and courage – together.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Let us SURPASS – Secure, United, Resilient – and ensure Singapore's safe passage through turbulent waters, today and for generations to come, and let us do so with a "we first" spirit, put our people, our families, our nation at the hearts of every step.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When we act with purpose, stand together and refuse to be passive, there is nothing we cannot achieve.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And let us remember even a small state like ours has agency, if we are careful and united.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In a world of shifting tides, Singapore must always strive to be useful but never made use of.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: President Tharman's call for unity, inclusivity and resilience deeply resonates with me, because these are not abstract ideals but real challenges we see on the ground.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: His Address is a timely reminder that while policies set the direction, it is a collective effort of Government, businesses, unions and our communities that will determine whether every Singaporean feels supported and included in this journey.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I am committed to do my part in Parliament and in my Nanyang division to help translate this vision into reality for our people.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Similarly, Prime Minister Mr Lawrence Wong had earlier voiced his concerns about vaping, especially those laced with harmful substances, during the National Day Rally.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: He affirmed the urgent need for stronger enforcement and harsher penalties.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: And true to his word, swift and decisive action followed, powerfully backed by our dedicated Home Team officers, working closely with MOH and HSA officers.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: What we are seeing now is the strength of a whole-of-Government response.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: A united front involving MOH, Ministry of Education (MOE), Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and MINDEF, is working to detect smuggling, and to protect our young people in schools, Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) and army camps.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: While I deeply wish this decisive move had come sooner to curb vaping's nasty spread, I am, nonetheless, grateful, for in matters of public health and safety, it is always better late than never.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: This very success, which demonstrates what we can achieve when agencies work in concert, brings me to my next point, the critical importance of seamless coordination within our Government to truly serve our people.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: We have come a long way since the famous "fish ball stick issue" was first raised in by then-backbencher Ms Low Yen Ling and mentioned by then-Prime Minister Mr Lee Hsien Loong during his National Day Rally in 2014.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Today, Ms Low Yen Ling is a Senior Minister of State, and inter-agency coordination has undoubtedly improved.
