text: My daughter, in her innocence, just said: "Mom, do what you can to help others." Their support carried me and carried me still because behind every volunteer, every MP, every Minister, there is a family that makes it possible for us to serve.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: For that, I remain deeply grateful to mine for the love, support and encouragement they have given unconditionally.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: People ask: "Why keep going back, week after week, for more than 20 years?" My answer is always the same.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It is the residents; it is the people.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Each story, each struggle, each glimmer of hope reminded me why service matters.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I remember sometime in May this year, a mother walked into my meet-the-people session, completely overwhelmed.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: She was caring for her elderly parents, while raising one special needs daughter and three others.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: She was exhausted, anxious, desperate, close to despair.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: That evening, together with my volunteers, we found her a simple solution, amongst a lot of other things – a rental flat to ease her immediate burden.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: So, what mattered more was not just the rental unit.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: What mattered was that she left knowing that she was not alone.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: She has a whole team of us behind us.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Months later, she came back to me, gave me a handmade flower and that itself touches me deeply.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: This gesture of gratitude will stay with me far longer than any appointment or anything or any title would ever bring.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Encounters like these remind me that politics is never an abstract.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It is not about paper-pushing or making grand speeches.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It is people, real people, real lives, and real struggles.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: And when we say "we first", not "me", this is what it looks like if everyone practises it.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Since the last GE in May, I have had the privilege of joining my team at more than 140 events.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Among them all, one moment stay deeply with me – it was my very first National Day Parade as an MP.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Standing at the Padang among the thousands of fellow Singaporeans, I was deeply moved by the sight of our people gathering as one.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: In that moment, the weight of this office truly struck me.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I felt the echoes of our beginnings, the unity, the sacrifice to build our nation, the solemn duty that we now have to carry to keep Singapore strong, united and moving forward.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: The voices of the crowd might rise beyond not just celebration.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: They were testimony to resilience, the resilience of a people who refused to give up, who believed we could build something out of nothing.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: In that same spirit, Mr Speaker, is what I see every week at our meet-the-people session.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Volunteers staying late in the night, helping, doing their best to help strangers.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: That, to me, is the Singapore spirit at its very best.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I often remind my volunteers: this work is never about us.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It is about the lives we touch, about the people.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I make that point to share with them, train them, build them, be with them so that we can serve and all of them have served, with confidence, because when I leave one, I leave the whole team and together, we grow stronger.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I have met mothers in their eighties still caring for their adult children with special needs.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I have met "sandwich-class" parents torn between their ageing parents and their young children in need.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: One mother told me; I totally agree: "I am always running but never arriving." Even in my own life, I have witnessed the quiet strength of caregiving networks.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Neighbours who notice those living alone alert my team, step in to watch over one another, offer simple acts of kindness without hesitation.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I have seen parents entrusting their children to neighbours during renovations.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: In my own experience, I was very, very late.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: My neighbours helped me to pick up my daughter.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: They helped me to feed her before I came home.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Like many Singaporean women, I wear many hats.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I am a daughter, wife, mother, employer, volunteer.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Menopause, mental fatigue, caregiving stress – these are real but very often dismissed or misunderstood.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: These are not an afterthought but our foundation of what we are going to do.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Just as we must support women in balancing their many responsibilities, we too must honour our seniors, who have carried their responsibilities for a lifetime.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: They are not merely dependents, but wisdom-keepers whose experiences continue to hold great value.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I recall meeting a resident who told me that he once served as a general manager of a company.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: He is now in his 60s, living alone.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Despite a lifetime of leadership and knowledge, he can only secure low-level jobs like security jobs.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Stories like his remind us that the skills and wisdom of our seniors are often undervalued, even as they still have so much to contribute.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I also recall attending the wake of an elderly man.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: The two of them, the man and his sister lived together in all their lives, unmarried.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: When she passed on, he was suddenly adrift and alone.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I connected him with support and encouraged him to come for volunteer and join our network.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Over time, I began to see light coming into his eyes again, a glimmer of hope.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Another time, I sat with a senior at a wake while he waited for a companion to arrive.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: All we did was just to keep him company.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: These encounters remind me that what our seniors often need is not grand gestures, but dignity, presence and inclusion.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Dignity in old age is not a luxury.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: And I will champion a Singapore where every senior can live with dignity, contribute with pride, and age with confidence with dignity.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: For more than two decades, I have walked the journey of the SMEs myself – balancing payroll, coping with rising costs, navigating layers of compliance and carrying the weight of employees who depend on me for their livelihoods.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I have seen business owners who are my friends quietly sacrifice family holidays, forgo their own salaries, dip into their savings – just to make sure the employees are paid.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: These stories rarely make the headlines, but they are the quiet sacrifices that keep Singapore's economy and communities going.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: This is why I will continue to press for clearer, more accessible forms of support for SMEs.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Support should not come hidden behind costly consultants or weighed down by red tape.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: They are strong – strong in heart, strong in resilience and strong in their contribution to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: For over 20 years, I have sat with residents at their lowest points, trained volunteers to serve better and built teams that believe in we, not me.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I see myself as a tiger mum not a bear mum, protective of every life entrusted to me, whether within my family or in the community I serve.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Just as I would never compromise on my children’s well-being, I will never compromise on protecting our heritage, our culture, our racial harmony that binds us all together.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I want Singapore and my constituents to know that I love what I do.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: In doing so, I hope to play my part in building a "we first" society that Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has called us forward.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: One day where every Singaporean can be the best version of ourselves and you are never left to walk alone.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I may be new but I bring with me the life experiences of many Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I look forward to working alongside all Members of this House to build a more compassionate, more cohesive, more courageous and more lovable Singapore.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: One that remains true to our values, confident in our future and united as one people.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: (In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, Mr Speaker, Singapore's racial and religious harmony, and the mutual trust and respect between families and society, are the result of 60 years of joint efforts by the PAP government, the people and religious groups.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Our forefathers have passed down this spirit to us today and we must carry it forward!

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: We must pass these important values from generation to generation.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Only by nurturing strong families and a caring society can we truly achieve the goals of "SG100".

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I am currently the Member of Parliament for Geylang Serai.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: It is a vibrant home with rich stories, traditions and history.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: The people here possess a strong "kampong" spirit, looking out for one another and caring for each other!

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: This is our Singaporean "kampong" spirit, and it is also an important driving force for Singapore to continue moving forward!

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I remember a resident who encountered housing and financial difficulties and came to seek my help.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Initially, she only told me that her husband had lost his job and the family's source of income had been cut off as a result.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: The family of four was staying with others, without a home of their own.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Their original plans to purchase a house had to be abandoned due to her husband's unemployment.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: Now, whenever this woman sees us, she will say "thank you".

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: This is the power of the "we" that the Prime Minister emphasises on.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: I say to you: "Come to me if you have a problem, ask me if you don't understand, I'm here for big and small issues." (In English): Mr Speaker, I support the Motion.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Fadli, you have a clarification to ask.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: If I understood it correctly, the Member acknowledged that though some people will be ahead and some will lag behind under a meritocracy, everyone will still be in the same direction of success on the escalator of progress.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: First, I think all of us care about those who are left behind.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: And on this, I just want to say, I think no one has a monopoly on compassion and on those who are left behind in society.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: I think all of us in this House we care about those who are left behind and we have been speaking up passionately on both sides of the House about those who have been left behind, so that is the first thing I would like to point out.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: And, indeed, Members on both sides of the House as well have in the previous terms of Parliament, in this term of Parliament made critiques about our meritocracy and suggested ways to improve our meritocracy.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: So, to answer Mr Fadli, am I satisfied with the state of meritocracy in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Just to make one more point of order.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Mr Fadli referred to me just now as Deputy Speaker.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Just want to be sure that I am speaking in my capacity as a MP now.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The President's address reminds us that our success as a nation cannot be measured by economic growth alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is also about how we support every Singaporean, young or old, to contribute and to live with dignity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We all play a part in creating communities of care that demonstrate compassion and ability to build common ground despite our varied experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This commitment to create communities of care should endure, even as our lives in Singapore become more digitalised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We must be committed to making sure that going digital helps every Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singaporeans should feel safe and respected in the digital space, and all of us, regardless of age, can look ahead with optimism and hope.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, digital technology has already woven itself into almost every aspect of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We access digital government services, use the Internet for school and work, shop online at our convenience and connect with loved ones through messaging apps and social media.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This reality brings both opportunities and challenges and we know that the digital transformation is not easy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Seniors feel overwhelmed, trying to keep up with new digital functions and apps.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some families face financial pressures regarding devices and Internet plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parents worry about the impact of screen time and what their children might encounter online especially with cyberbullying becoming increasingly prevalent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our young people feel anxious and stressed by the pressures and comparisons that social media can amplify in their daily lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: All of us, regardless of age, have probably been caught off guard by increasingly realistic fake content that is becoming harder to identify.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These concerns are real and they matter to us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have a long-standing commitment to support our seniors and low-income families in their digitalisation journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: She was scared that she would not be able to catch up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: So, when she found out about the SDO's training programmes from a digital ambassador during a community event, she decided to give it a try.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: After attending the programmes, she gained the skills and today she can confidently use e-payments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: More and more of our seniors are going online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While it is also true that there are some seniors who are put off by the fear of being scammed online, the guidance at the SDO programmes help address the concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In these programmes, they are also taught how to recognise suspicious links or offers online and build healthy digital habits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is inspiring to watch them overcome their fears, adopt a positive attitude and embrace new digital technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We also understand that not everyone is ready or able to go fully digital and that is okay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is why we have kept alternatives, like physical CDC vouchers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Residents who need assistance with Government digital transactions can continue to get in-person assistance at Government agencies' physical service touchpoints.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They can also visit ServiceSG Centres for assistance with 600 frequently-used Government services and schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We encourage digital-first but will not be digital-only.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to help citizens access Government services through whatever means they prefer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Students now get hands-on experience with AI technology, where they can learn to use generative AI for brainstorming and creating content, while understanding how to use it safely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: And this learning journey extends beyond schools and beyond just teaching the young.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Earlier this week, I spoke on how libraries serve as places where we can learn new knowledge and exchange ideas with people who have similar interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Two years ago, he attended a one-day workshop at MakeIT, the library makerspace in Punggol Regional Library, to learn the basics of 3D printing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The workshop sparked his interest in 3D printing as he could see his ideas brought to life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Recently, he has expanded his skills to include Gen AI tools for advanced designs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Every week, Mr Ronnie returns to the library to create puzzles and toys for his grandchildren, hoping to kindle the same creative passion in them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At MakeIT, he also met people with similar interests and enjoyed exchanging ideas and tips with fellow members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ronnie's experience captures the spirit of our libraries as places to spark curiosity, equalise access to technologies and strengthen community through learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond libraries, learning also takes place at over 50 Digital Clubs that have been set up by People's Association Active Ageing Councils and SDO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These Digital Clubs promote peer learning and seniors are encouraged to learn from one another because, sometimes, the best teacher is the person sitting next to you who just recently figured something out and remembers how confusing it felt at first.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Having access to technology and knowing how to use it is important but there is another piece of the puzzle that is equally crucial.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Digital services should feel intuitive and easy to use for all users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Most of us find them quite easy to use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But Mr Ng Choon Hwee, 70, who has a visual impairment, faces a very different experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: He uses the voiceover function to tell him what is on the screen but if a banking app is not properly labelled, the voiceover reads out unhelpful descriptions, like "button" or "image", that does not allow him to perform the task that he intends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A straightforward task like checking his bank balance or reviewing transactions becomes a frustrating guessing game.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond incorporating inclusive design features that serve users with special needs, a well-designed app enhances usability for all of us, regardless of age or ability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The new standards guide developers in aspects of digital accessibility so that digital Government services are compatible with assistive technology and are easier to use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are also actively involving citizens in improving user experience of digital Government services and ensuring such services are accessible to all.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A key part of this effort is our Tech Kaki community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Tech Kaki brings together citizens from all walks of life who share their experiences and insights to help us design better Government digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Such efforts contribute to ensuring the app is accessible to all Singaporeans, to support them in living healthily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our hope is that whether it is applying for housing, booking a doctor's appointment, or seeking social support services, the experience should be smooth and reassuring for all users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Accessible digital design is about more than just lines of code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It represents our shared commitment to building an equitable, thriving environment where everyone can take part confidently and with ease.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Now, I would address something that has been weighing on many of our minds – keeping our online spaces safe and welcoming for everyone, especially for our children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In addition to the threat of misinformation and disinformation, we are seeing the troubling rise in online harms and negative online behaviour.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To better protect Singaporeans from online harms, we have been strengthening our regulatory tools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For instance, the Broadcasting Act was amended to allow us to enhance online safety of Online Communication Services (OCSs), which, at present, comprise social media services (SMS) and app distribution services (ADS), also known as the app stores.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The amended Broadcasting Act grants the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) the legal powers to issue directions to disable access by Singapore users to egregious content found on OCSs, such as content depicting child sexual exploitation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Furthermore, the amendment also provides IMDA with the legal powers to issue Codes of Practice to require designated social media platforms and app stores to put in place systems and processes to mitigate the risks of exposure to harmful content for all Singapore users, especially for children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to review our legislation and build necessary regulatory safeguards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are already studying approaches taken in jurisdictions, like the United Kingdom, European Union (EU) and Australia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In particular, we are looking at the implementation of age assurance measures in these places to guide our own efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are engaging social media platforms, think tanks, technology vendors to understand the space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We want to put in place effective legislation that can protect our children from harmful and inappropriate content online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, legislative levers alone cannot create the kind of safe and trusted online community we want to live in.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For that to happen, we each must play our part to build a culture of respect and kindness in our shared digital space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I am encouraged by how families are stepping up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parenting in the digital era comes with real challenge and I see parents putting in their best efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond stronger legislation, parents wanted access to relevant resources, such as online courses, guides and workshops, that can help them manage their child's digital activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These resources will be tailored according to the various stages in the parenting journey, based on their child's developmental age range and their experiences with key digital milestones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, first exposure to screens, first phone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We want to support parents in cultivating healthy digital habits in their children from a young age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, creating a positive online culture is not just about parents and children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Every single one of us contributes to shaping our shared digital space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Maybe before we share that post, we can pause and consider how our words might affect someone else.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: When we see cyberbullying happening, perhaps we could report it instead of scrolling past silently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These might feel like small gestures, but they will shape the digital culture we are all part of.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As many in this House have alluded to, building a "we first" society starts with "me".

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The vision of an inclusive digital society is a shared responsibility that requires us to all lean in.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We would like to invite community partners to help support digital parenting in this ever-changing landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We encourage companies and agencies to adopt accessible digital design practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: And as individuals, we can help a neighbour or family member with picking up a new digital skill, model positive use of technology for our children and simply choosing kindness in our online interactions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Together, we can build a Smart Nation that genuinely serves everyone, not just those who are digitally-savvy, but all of us, with our different abilities and needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The digital future is inevitable, but the kind of digital future we create is entirely up to us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Let us make it one we can all be proud of.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Cai Yinzhou, you have a clarification to make?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I rise in support of the Motion of Thanks for the President's address.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is a privilege for me to join this debate as a new Member.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: First, I would like to thank the residents of Tengah and Chua Chu Kang for giving me the opportunity to speak in the 15th Parliament.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am also immensely grateful to my better half and my two-year-old for their unwavering love.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And to my team and volunteers, thank you for being my second family.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Last week, I watched my two-year-old play with gears, and it reminded me of how healthcare and research are like the hidden gears behind a masterfully crafted clock.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: You do not always see them, but they keep life moving – quietly, precisely, relentlessly.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Each gear must be aligned; each spring must be wound with care.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If even one falters, a missed diagnosis, a delayed study, the whole system stutters.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Today, I would like to speak on two areas that are deeply intertwined with our future: healthcare and research.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is no longer solely about life and death.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is about how we live in old age and in sickness, and the quality of life we can sustain across the lifespan.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This shift in focus brings urgency to how we manage downstream healthcare, supporting those already living with illness, especially within our growing population of older citizens.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Judicious allocation of resources will determine whether our healthcare standards remain sustainable and continue to improve.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Importantly, downstream care is not just about ageing.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It encompasses a broader spectrum of lived experiences: the young adult recovering from a stroke; the parent managing a child’s autism diagnosis; the worker coping with chronic pain; the caregiver supporting both ageing parents and young children.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To meet these diverse and increasing demands while upholding healthcare quality, we need to continually review how care is delivered.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is already standard in countries like the UK.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Outside hospitals and within our communities, engaging seniors meaningfully can be key to optimising their physical and mental health.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Rather than seeing seniors as passive recipients of care, we should recognise senior volunteerism as a strategic asset.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Regardless of age, mobility, or technology proficiency; whether they use a wheelchair, a tongkat, or none at all – we can all actively welcome seniors into care initiatives through volunteer networks.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This unlocks a win-win: seniors gain purpose and connection, while communities benefit from their care and experience.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To enhance its impact, I suggest: moving beyond reactive screening by offering guidance on postural health and ergonomics from early school-going age; embedding early touchpoints into antenatal care to equip first-time parents with tools for building healthy routines from the start; redesigning existing spaces in HDB estates to include multi-use play corners that encourage outdoor activity, family bonding and intergenerational engagement.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Besides care recipients, caregivers are an integral part of the healthcare landscape.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore has laid the groundwork for caregiving support through subsidies, respite services and community programmes.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But the caregiving landscape is evolving and we must elevate our approach.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is not one role, but many – nurse, planner, advocate, emotional anchor.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To truly elevate support, we should involve caregiving-trained professionals in policy, programme design and decision-making; and individuals who understand care from the inside out.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If done right, caregiving support should be precise, efficient and impactful.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I will begin with research strategy, followed by research impact assessment.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must ask: what are we building and who are we becoming?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We cannot simply cruise along with the flow of the waters; we need to accelerate and ride with the waves – as the Chinese saying goes, "不随波逐流，要乘风破浪".

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In a world of rapid innovation, drifting with the current may seem safe, but it leaves us vulnerable to external tides.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If we only follow, we risk becoming dependent on others for the technologies and solutions that shape our future.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We are not striving to be sellers of everything, but we cannot afford to be buyers of everything either.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Take the current trend of AI as an example.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: When policy and innovation move together with clarity and courage, Singapore will not only keep pace with the waves of innovation.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We will set our own direction, chart a course others can follow and build capabilities that serve our people and economy for decades to come.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must ensure that funding is not merely meeting check-box criteria, but delivering real impact.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are we solving the problems we set out to solve?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are we plugging the gaps that matter most?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We often measure success by volume; papers published, grants awarded, partnerships signed.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These are important, but they do not always reflect whether the work is transformative or relevant.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must also be mindful of the administrative workload on researchers.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: When too much time is spent on compliance and reporting, we risk shifting focus away from innovation.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Accountability is essential, but it must be proportionate and purposeful.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And we need research-trained professionals, not just those with degrees, but those with deep, discipline-based expertise to manage and evaluate research outcomes.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But there is much more to speak on, and beneath these diverse topics, lies a common thread.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We are all in it together, each with different personalities, backgrounds and perspectives.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There is no right or wrong in who we are.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What matters is that we row in the same direction.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In healthcare, in research, in every policy we shape, we must choose the right way, not the easy way.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The right way demands courage, clarity and compassion.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It asks us to listen deeply, act boldly and build patiently.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is inspired by the Prime Minister's National Day Rally speech and the President's Parliamentary address.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin): We are not passengers — we are crew.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Each with a different rhythm, a different strength.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But the boat moves only when we row together.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Let us choose the right way, not the easy way.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Let us move as many, but sail as one.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen
text: I just wanted to explain that I used it in the context of a story I was relating and did not mean to be unparliamentary.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Many colleagues here have spoken about a turbulent world; great-power contest, technological disruption.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: From Singapore's early days, we have known these dangers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We have always, and often been caught sometimes by ourselves, as an improbable nation, a little red dot.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This labels emphasise our vulnerability, too small to matter, too exposed to survive alone, too young to develop deep roots.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Yet, these weaknesses force us to build deeper foundations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Large nations can tolerate institutional decay, we cannot.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Large nations can indulge in identity politics, we cannot.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Our vulnerability has became our vigilance and our constraints become our discipline.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And from this foundation, something remarkable has emerged as we began a new chapter under our fourth Prime Minister, even amidst a dangerous world, we have a basis for optimism that is often overlooked.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We have quietly emerged as a civilisation of states, rare among small nations born not of design, but of decisions under pressure.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Like the Venetian Republic of old, small in territory, immense in influence, because Venice knew what it stood for.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Venice proved that civilisational death does not require vast lands.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We are more than a flag and anthem.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Our institutions are trusted, our common purpose and values are clear.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We possess the cultural maturity and sovereign worldview to set our own compass.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And in this dangerous age, while others fracture, we unite.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Therefore, let us build on a new source of strength: the quiet stature of an emerging civilisational state; small on the map, large in mind and spirit.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: To tap on this strength, we can tell our story better, harness technological disruption, keep life affordable and expand our capacity for care.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: If Singapore is a ship, our media is the rudder that allows us to reflect together, to steer our collective destiny.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And our culture is our ballast, keeping us steady through choppy waters.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: To tell our stories better, we must do four things.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Yes, AI can write prose and automate workflows.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: But journalism is fundamentally about human connection – reporters engaging in people and uncovering stories that matter.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We are not just maintaining standards; we are polishing diamonds.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Zaobao is already the most respected Chinese media outlet globally.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And CNA commands credibility far beyond our shores.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: With strategic investment, can we position Business Times as the Financial Times of Southeast Asia?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: In an era where great powers project, not just hard power, but influence, our media is our best vehicle for soft power; offering an authentic Singapore perspective to the world.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Two, we need to build the generational divide by connecting our youths to our media and culture, for without this connection, our cultural future dims.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Fortunately, I can see green shoots are emerging.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Zaobao's recent partnership with Chinese media company, they are the creators of this web novel turned hit drama series called "Yu Qing Nian", it is a fantastic drama series.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This contest a partnership has generated, I was told, tens of thousands of entries from all over the world, including from Singapore and the region.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: MediaCorp's “Superstar” and SPH's “Xing Kong Xin” are discovering new voices and new lyrics that speak to our people.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This two-way bridge helps our media feel the pulse of our younger generations while nurturing future newsmakers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Third, we should refresh and extend the Singapore story.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Past cultural icons, like Liang Wen Fu and Stefanie Sun, have shaped our identity with minimal Government support.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Give them the resources and access to our ecosystem to write the next chapter of our story.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Because we should think about the consequences of letting our cultural development languish.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: In 10 years, will we accept our identity being shaped by the occasional Netflix drama done by a foreign content creator?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Will we be comfortable if we let others, including those with an agenda, decide what to amplify or diminish about our Singapore culture?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: In my view, we should enforce MOH's guidelines on healthy social media consumption for our youths.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Because we should also count the the cost of inaction?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Without further decisive action, our youths' mental health will continue to be affected.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Algorithms, not us, will shape our collective consciousness.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Most of all, when one is drowning in newsfeeds personalised to the “I” and the “I” here is defined by the shortest possible attention span, what space are we leaving to build a “we first” society?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Yes, we all know that AI-driven disruptions are both creating opportunities and challenges.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: These displaced technology talents do not just disappear.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: They diffuse into other industries and bring with them the skills with them to spark broader productivity and Singapore should seize these opportunities as well.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: While private companies shed tech jobs, we should accelerate digitalisation instead.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Hire young IT graduates to supercharge Ministries with AI, prototype solutions and help companies cut costs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: In short, we should transform job disruption into opportunity.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Third, we should reskill and retool our education system.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We all know that in this age, tech talent needs three things: a deep understanding of system architecture depth, business knowledge and AI coding ability.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: It means that our senior project managers must relearn coding to be able to harness AI effectively.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Our universities and polytechnics must provide tech students with business classes and industry projects.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We must try hard to create pivot programmes for tech students and recent graduates into high-demand areas, such as AI development and cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And finally, we must prepare for broader waves.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: AI automation will spread everywhere, be it self-driving vehicles or delivery robots.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This will ensure that disruption does not lead to distress.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Three, keep homes and daily lives within reach.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I welcome the brisk pace of BTO constructions, adding supply would moderate resale pressure.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: With more homes coming, we should be able to expand both access and affordability.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I hope we can consider raising income ceilings for high-achieving Singaporeans with limited inter-generational wealth and also allow Singaporeans married to foreigners, older applicants from private estates and singles to access larger BTOs and not just resale flats.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I hope we can also consider lowering the singles eligibility age by two years.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: These are not concessions; we should recognise that diverse family structures deserve equal dignity in housing.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: It is the daily cost of living in our daily lives.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We all know that coffee shop prices where it is now leads to high rental rates and I hope the Government can intervene directly.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Let us consider targeted purchases of surrounding shops and converting them into Government-owned Community Canteens, we can call it "⼈民⾷堂".

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We are talking about low-cost spaces, tendered to operators who commit to fair prices and quality meals.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And I believe that we just need a limited number of them, perhaps 20 or 30 sites throughout Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I believe these will do much to taper excessive coffee shop prices.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: My final point is about enlarging our circle of care.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: A good example is how global crises such as the plight of civilians in Gaza has moved Singaporeans across all races and faiths to help.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: In fact, they are preparing for four more projects in Gaza and the West Bank.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: The Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) airdrops supplies and convenes the Humanitarian Assistance Disaster Response conference, which I have attended over the last few years and I saw how SAF brought together militaries and volunteer welfare organisations to respond faster when crises strike.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: So, this example shows how the hearts of Singaporeans have expanded beyond our shores.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I hope that the same expansive spirit must also transform care at home in Singapore, in three ways.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I hope we can strengthen our oral care.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Dental health remains an area of improvement in our otherwise excellent healthcare system.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Let us consider creating a Healthier SG dental plan by working with private sector dental clinics.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Two, we must accelerate a nationwide roll-out of affordable assisted living for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: For many of our seniors, our current senior care model assumes binary choices, either full independence with lived-in help or institutional care.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Therefore, I hope we can quickly conclude our learnings from the pilot that is going on, about shared resources for assisted living and scale it nationwide.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: How we treat the voiceless reveals our values.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: As cruelty reports rise, we must respond decisively.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Strengthen penalties and give agencies resources for swift action.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And I will follow up in subsequent debates with detailed proposals.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Many countries struggle to be more than a flag and an anthem, united in name, divided in purpose.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We have developed the habits of a civilisational state, institutions that keep faith, a culture that renews, a people who hold together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We often associate such a death of large nations like France, yet size is not destiny.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Like Venice once did, Singapore shows that a small state can carry a civilisation.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: This is my first time speaking in this House, and I do so with gratitude, humility and a full heart.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I treasure the chance to speak up on behalf of other regular Singaporeans, just like myself.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I come to this Chamber with a commitment to listen, to care and to take action.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I wish to express my appreciation to all those who have served in this House before me.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Their dedication has shaped the Singapore we live in today.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: It is now our turn to continue that work with conviction, compassion and courage.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: The President reminded us, in his address, that we are at a critical juncture in our nation’s journey.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: We were reminded that the world around us is changing in profound way and uncertainty is becoming the new normal.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: By strengthening our security, transforming our economy, sustaining mobility and putting "we" before "me", we can chart our course with confidence and unity.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: A Chinese saying has guided me in my journey as a volunteer and now as an MP, "老吾老，以及人之老; 幼吾幼，以及人之幼." To honour the elderly as we do so for our elderly at home and care for others' children as we care for our own.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: We all know of some aunties who live alone and almost never leave the house, or uncles sitting by themselves with their kopi at coffeeshops, watching the world move past them, growing quieter every day.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I think about my own grandmother and the older neighbours who watched me grow up.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Many of them want to feel connected to the community they are in.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: They want to play their part in the community.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: They want to feel like they still matter.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: She is a retiree and often organises seniors' exercise sessions in the Nee Soon community.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: She also encourages the group to have potluck sessions during festive celebrations.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Today, the group has grown to 50 seniors.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: There could be many more warm-hearted elderly, just like Mdm Ho, in our community.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: We should support such ground-up efforts and share them with the broader community.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Growing old should not feel like growing invisible. "家有一老，如有一宝" (elders in a family are like treasures) should not be just lip service.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Our seniors are a gift, not a burden to be managed.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: But we must do more to reimagine what ageing can look like; where seniors are fully present, where they mentor, share or shape their communities.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Imagine primary schools where seniors come to read to students, share stories of the olden days or simply help with co-curricular activities.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Imagine void decks with community kitchens, where older folks share their family recipes with the younger residents.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: All these are not grand policy moves, but they build connection and connection is what keeps people going.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Let us also look at our common areas.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Community gardening, music corners where young and old can perform together.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: These are small ideas that add a soft touch to our daily lives.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: As our services transition online, we must ensure our seniors are not locked out.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I have seen elderly persons struggle to book polyclinic appointments or get flustered accessing Government services on their phones.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: The answer is not to tell them to catch up, but it is to walk with them, one gentle step at a time.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I hope these can be further expanded to include peer learning, where digitally savvy seniors guide their fellow neighbours or pairing youths with seniors as an intergenerational activity.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: At the heart of this is a simple principle: ageing well is not just about living longer; it is about living with purpose and joy.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: These are the youths who do not always show up in statistics.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: They may skip class, drift into the wrong company, or simply stop believing they have a future.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I did not know who to look for or where to look for help.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I mixed with the wrong company and got into all kinds of trouble during my secondary school days.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Essentially, I became one of those kids that parents tell their children to stay away from.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Thankfully, my secondary school teachers had an abundance of patience, guidance and belief that every student can grow and succeed.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Thanks to them, I managed to turn my way around.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Some of us here may be familiar with IMPARTSG.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: It is a charitable organisation whose core mission is to give youths facing adversity a fighting chance.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: IMPARTSG supported Narish through his "N" level as a private candidate and his subsequent traineeship at ITE.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Thereafter, Narish returned to intern at the organisation, driven by his passion to empower others facing similar challenges.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: In 2023, IMPARTSG sponsored Narish for a Work-Study Diploma programme in Community Engagement and Development.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Due to the trauma, Albert suffered from severe anxiety, school refusal and social isolation.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Narish approached him with empathy and created a safe space and developed a plan to integrate Albert's love for sepak takraw with his social reintegration.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Today, Albert flourishes as a regular community volunteer working with seniors on Age Well programmes.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Narish's story reminds us of the collective potential we unlock when we invest in our youths and empower them to uplift others.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: This is real transformative power when we come together for common good.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: There are many others like the old "me" and Narish in our community.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I also believe we need to continue broadening the definition of success for our youths.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: And we can all play a part too.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: It could be a hawker stall uncle who gives a teen a weekend job; a teacher who checks in after class; a grassroots leader who listens without judgement; when we wrap a net of care around our youth, they fall less and climb more.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: A young person who feels seen, who feels believed in, will rise to the challenge.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: We just have to give them the room to do so.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, I hope Singapore can do more for our elderly, enabling them to participate in building our community cohesion.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: We do not necessarily need large-scale policies, but rather through some creative community programmes, such as making good use of public spaces, allowing them to enter schools and community kitchens and so forth, to build relationships with the younger generation, and live fulfilling and active lives.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I also hope we can continue our efforts to walk alongside our elderly step by step on the digitalisation journey.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Our young people, especially marginalised youth, also need more help.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that programmes designed for young people can be developed with more long-term stable resources, allowing them to help each other and realise their potential together.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Young people should also continue to have more pathways to success, letting them know that "heaven has endowed everyone with talents for eventual use".

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: As long as we believe in their abilities, they, too, will learn to believe in themselves.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I believe that as long as we take good care of our older generation and our young people, we can link the past with the future, and together, make Singapore not just only a more prosperous, but also more heartwarming place. : In conclusion, Mr Speaker, Sir, the President reminded us that Singapore must uphold trust, deepen unity and ensure that progress is inclusive.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I believe unity happens when people feel they belong.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Our seniors want to know that they are not being left behind in a fast-changing world.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Our struggling youths want to believe they still have a chance.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: If we take care of both, we secure our past and protect our future.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I hope to see a Singapore where generations do not live apart but grow together, where community is not just a slogan, but something we feel every time we step into a lift, or a hawker centre, or a park.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: I am new to this House and I promise from the onset that I will do the work, I will listen to those whose voices tremble, I will speak up when silence becomes too loud.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: And I will always remember why I am here, not for myself, but for those who gave me this seat.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: But I hope we will also be known for our empathy.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: That, to me, is real progress, not just being the best, but being good.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: As we reflect on the President's address, one message rings clear.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The 14th Parliament started in the middle of a COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The 15th Parliament began a new chapter with a sea of economic turbulence.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: President Tharman spoke directly to our lived realities as we ride this tide of change: youths seeking meaningful jobs, families navigating rising costs and caregiving pressures, seniors hoping for joyful and fulfilling lives.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The President and Prime Minister also spoke on how we must always put "we" before "me", because the strength of Singapore lies in how we care, uplift and stand together.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I believe that this starts with everyday care across all life stages, from zero to 100, is the next step in our journey to a "we first" society.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We must become a society where our progress is measured, not by prosperity, but by how we care for one another, a Singapore where persons at any milestone are cared for as they grow up or grow old.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: First, everyday care in a "we first" society starts with caring for our seniors.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: As a community volunteer for more than 15 years, I have had the opportunity and privilege to journey with and witness first-hand the strength and contributions of our seniors.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It is now our turn, my turn, to take care for them in their silver years.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: As we adapt to an ageing population, our seniors must be able to live with dignity, security, and purpose.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Accessibility is a priority for me in Nee Soon South.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We can do more to make our public spaces, transport, and housing more senior-friendly.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We must also invest more in upstream preventative healthcare, encouraging independent living, healthy lifestyles, early intervention and a closely-knit community.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: In Nee Soon South, there is always an activity for our seniors, every day.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: At my house visits, I am inspired to see our seniors doing their part to age well.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: One of them is 85-years-young Mdm Tay, who has been selling fishball noodles at Peiying Primary School for 62 years and counting.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Or a Mr Sim who runs five kilometres at 78 years old every single day.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: As a government, we must not only support active seniors such as Mdm Tay and Mr Sim but also reach out to other seniors and empower them to age well too.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Second, everyday care in a "we first" society starts with caring for our young in schools.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: But, for many students, their formative years consist of a high-pressure race through the schooling system, with the end goal of getting good grades, entering a good university and finding a good job.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Learning feels like an obstacle they have to overcome to achieve a narrow definition of success focused on academic grades.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: As we prepare our young for a world with technology like AI, they need to be equipped with more than grades to survive.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Success in school should also be defined by developing their ability to learn and grow.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: This cannot be learnt by memorising facts from a textbook.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Instead, it must be cultivated through students' active and willing participation.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: They must learn to embrace the discomfort that comes with navigating uncertain situations outside structured classrooms.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: An education system in which students enjoy learning does not mean lower standards or less rigorous curriculums.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: By evaluating students based on processes over outcomes, it encourages students to take on greater challenges.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: A caring society for our schooling youths also means taking action to help them overcome challenges of mental health and bullying.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: They are struggling silently, as a sizeable group does not seek any professional help.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I hope to support more safe spaces for youths to express their struggles to trusted adults and peers.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: By teaching our children to support those around them, we create a culture where mental health struggles are not perceived as a diminishing of one's capabilities and value, but a challenge that can be overcome with community support to allow every person to realise their full potential.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: To all our boys and girls sitting for PSLE, do your best and know that your best is good enough.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Third, everyday care in a "we first" society also means caring for those who might be at the peak of their health but face less obvious challenges.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I call them senior youths, not young seniors, but senior youths – Singaporeans in their mid-20s to mid-30s.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: These are young Singaporeans who are burdened with adulting responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: They have just entered the workforce, just got married, just started their parenthood journey.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: They are finding their footing in today's uncertain world with a rapidly changing economic order but also bearing the responsibility of being caregivers to their children and/or senior parents.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: In interacting with our senior youths, and being one myself, I understand how their high aspirations are met with real anxieties.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Senior youths aspire to have fulfilling careers and give their families a good life and have anxiety over job security as they hear the increasing challenges for graduates to secure a job in the face of economic headwinds.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Senior youths aspire to be good parents and filial children, but face the anxiety of balancing caregiving responsibilities with work responsibility.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: On workplaces, these need not come at the expense of productivity.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Our tripartite framework tells us that it is never a zero-sum game between our workers and our companies.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: They require a Government that is willing to broker conversations and provide leadership, a union that is sensitive to the needs of workers, and companies that are willing to experiment and provide feedback.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Sometimes, the process of arriving at these solutions might seem slow, but I believe that in building a truly compassionate society, it is necessary that we pause to hear one another out, and each of us in this House can play our part in ensuring that Singaporeans we care about are heard and their concerns addressed.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Fourth, everyday care in a "we first" society starts with caring for our animals too.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I have had the privilege to see the quiet but powerful ways animals and animal lovers bring our community together.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: From a Nee Soon Pets Fiesta attended by 3,000 animal lovers just over the weekend to the quiet dedication of a network of community feeders who brave rain or shine to care for our community animals, these reflect something larger: a kinder, more caring home.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Coincidentally, just as Minister of State Alvin Tan who met the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA) team in July, I also had the chance to visit their Sungei Tengah premises where I met Halia, a gentle community dog and she was ready for adoption at that time.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Just about two weeks ago, SPCA's Executive Director, Mr Walter Leong, shared with me that Halia had been adopted and found her forever home.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It is about the kind of society we want to build, one that values life.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
