text: But it is my belief that we are here to catalyse a brighter future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Dr Koh, do you have a clarification to make?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Foo Cexiang, do you have a clarification to make?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have a clarification to make with regard to the hon Member Mr Kenneth Tiong's speech.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Two quick clarifications just to make sure I do not mischaracterise what he has shared.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The first, is he suggesting that the Singapore Government should be entering a domain or a partnership with some of our regional Governments in partnership to develop as what he described, a similar model of whatever was the collaboration between the English and the French?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, the first is he suggesting that the Singapore Government collaborate with governments in the region to develop an industry?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The second one and he also made this point quite clearly that the Government should not crowd out the space for SMEs.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But at the same time he also shared that for this initial project, the Government must play an important role and then develop the system of SMEs, the ecosystem of SMEs underneath it.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, maybe for me to understand better, what is this sector that he has in mind?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: That the Government will not play a role whereby it oversteps the role of SMEs, but is able to create an ecosystem for SMEs in collaboration with governments in the region?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: On the second clarification, on which sectors that it should be in.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Certainly, there are many, many areas of strength that I think are in Southeast Asia.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: And I think generally the principle is that it really depends on if the Government is in a position to shape these markets internationally, for the benefit of this country , it should.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: Could I just venture a step further to ask the Member whether he could share with us some of the countries or governments he has in mind that, in his view, we should be collaborating with in terms of some of the sectors that he has raised?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I brought up one example in my speech.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I say that that is one possible direction, regarding semi-conductors.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: But of course, I do not want to be overly prescriptive about the nature of the industry.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I think there are many potential areas that could be developed.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: But I guess the root of the question I am asking is that, in his view, there are governments in the region that will be able to partner us meaningfully in such an endeavour.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: The level of the region, where they are, the resources that they have, the manpower they have, the skills that they have, there will be a meaningful collaboration that we can have with them.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: That is the question I have for the Member.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: There are many sources of industrial strength in Southeast Asia.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Again, as I said, I think this Government has a prerogative to decide what these areas should be and to see how best to develop these, but certainly I do not want to be overly prescriptive in what it could be.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: But I know it is easier said than done, especially when success seems out of reach; and the people who are in the position to make a difference seem out of touch.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I sense some among us may be feeling this way: unsure, uncertain, overwhelmed.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: This too, shall pass, and with hardship comes ease.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: But let me say this: I believe in the power of the youth, so do not give up on you.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I believe in the power of family, do not give up on each other.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I believe in the power of unity, so let us do this together.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: With this same voice, I thank our families, our volunteers and Singapore's patriots who rally with us to build a Singapore we can all be proud of.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The privilege, expectations and "amanah", or responsibility, standing right here right now, is not lost on me.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Today, I will take you on a journey to envision the Singapore I hope to build in three parts, using three proverbs, and in three other languages.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: First, in our National Language, Mr Speaker, in Malay, please. :   The strength of the people, is in its unity.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: A Singapore that is strong, united and cohesive.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: A Singapore that supports one another during difficult times.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: That is my hope for Singapore and for our community.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: For 15 years, I reported the stories of our community as an editor and presenter for Mediacorp News.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I was fortunate because through my career, I had the privilege of preserving our culture and language and connecting with our community.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I also served for more than a decade in charitable organisations, such as PPIS (Singapore Muslim Women's Association) – helping those in need amongst us and in several national councils and associations – representing the voice and aspirations of our community.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I have never missed any opportunity to contribute because I truly believe that success, values, and aspirations; all begin at home.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Therefore, I hope the Government continues to work hand in hand with Malay/Muslim organisations, social service agencies, as well as the private sector, making holistic efforts to strengthen and empower our families, so that no one is left behind.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Sometimes, when tackling complex problems, there seems to be no clear solutions, no examples, no templates.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: For instance, a Fengshan resident, Mr O, is a father with a heart condition.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: He is no longer working and must care for two children – one studying at MINDS and another who has eczema, a type of skin ailment.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Additionally, his wife is receiving long-term treatment in hospital due to stroke.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: When he came to us, Mr O was quite at a loss.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Essentially, our team used a holistic approach that took into account the specific characteristics of each family, which is providing assistance while empowering them.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Family and community stability, as well as a united people, are also important indicators of success – especially in uncertain times, when tensions between nations are escalating.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Recently, I had the opportunity to join President Tharman Shanmugaratnam's delegation for his State Visit to Egypt – for the very first time.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Singapore's reputation as a trusted, respected and forward-looking country was clearly evident.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The President's visit demonstrated both the importance of expanding our networks and Singapore's significant role on the world stage.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: During the visit, I had the chance to meet four Gaza residents who were receiving medical treatment in Egypt, together with a team of Singaporean doctors and nurses who were specially flown in to provide treatment – the first foreign team given permission to work in an Egyptian hospital.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Therefore, Singapore must remain steadfast and firm in helping victims of war and continue to speak up for the oppressed.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Singaporeans harbour hope that Singapore will assume a greater role and take a clearer stance on the Gaza conflict.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: While in Egypt, I was also deeply moved after meeting Singaporean students studying at the Al-Azhar University.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: They possess tremendous spirit and are committed to flying the Singapore flag high.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Solidarity is the harmony of different voices, with varying tones and rhythms flowing together, united for the same purpose.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: A nurturing environment is important for someone to flourish.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The family is like a garden that must be carefully tended, so that life's resources are shared as fairly as possible, and nothing is hidden in the shadows.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: We can be anchors of progress and beacons of unity.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I will strive to ensure that our children grow up with confidence, our youth receive opportunities and our families believe in a brighter future. : Mr Speaker, in Mandarin, please, especially, for my Fengshan residents.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: (In Mandarin):   "Care for our own elderly and extend that care to the elderly of others" – what a beautiful saying!

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Many of our elderly shy from asking their families for help, fearing they might trouble others.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I hope we can proactively extend a helping hand and do our part for our elders, so they can enjoy a meaningful and dignified life. : Mr Speaker, we are where we are because of the giants before us.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Trail blazers who cleared the path, smashed ceilings and cleaned sticky floors.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Singapore must be a safe space for our elderlies who have done so much to build the Singapore we are privileged to live in now.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: During the National Day Rally, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, shared a photo of my Fengshan resident, Mdm Wong celebrating her 100th birthday.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I met her the same week, to show her how many Singaporeans celebrated with her.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: She was in high-spirits, all smiles and said, "阿嬤开心!" or Grandma is happy.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Joy keeps Mdm Wong going and many super-aged seniors too.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I hope for our seniors to truly age well, on site and with dignity.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I hope for a Singapore where our elderlies know they can depend on their families for support.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I hope for the Government to better support families with elderly, especially the ones who also have young children as well.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: On my house visits, I often meet seniors who live alone.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: At Fengshan, we take note of these homes.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Our grassroots leader and I make time to engage and stay in touch.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: We organise luncheons and gatherings and encourage them to have an active social life.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The work of the Active Ageing Centres, the Active Ageing Centre befrienders and the Silver Generation Office is becoming more important, to ensure our seniors living alone are not isolated.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: And I look forward to greater synergies among all our initiatives so seniors have one single point of contact for community care, so they can focus on living their golden years meaningfully and with dignity.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Next, very briefly in Tamil, please, Mr Speaker. :   The continuous crawling of ants can wear out even a rock.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: There is so much we can learn from this saying.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I have not learnt enough of it, but one day, I will. : The proverb, even ants can wear out a rock, speaks of the perseverance and resilience I hope for Singapore and our youths to possess.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: A Singapore where our young feel heard, seen and where they matter.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: A Singapore where our young are motivated and do not give up.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: A Singapore where our young feel like they belong.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Economic uncertainty and social pressures are on the up and up.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: One of the concerns of young Singaporeans is employment.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: It is unfortunate that the pressure to get a job meant young people are racing to stack internships.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I believe it is important for the young to discover themselves.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I started my career as a journalist, crossed over to public affairs, found meaning in social impact and embraced a new opportunity in advisory consulting.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: For Singaporeans to embody lifelong learning, there must also be a mindset shift of embracing lifelong support.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I shared the anxiety of our young, but also their drive for making the world a better place for the next generation.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I share their purpose on being good and doing right.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I will continue to listen to our young and give them space to untangle, deconstruct and undo what does not quite work.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I recently met some youths based in Cairo, having just returned from a State Visit with the President to Egypt and I am filled with immense pride at how our youths are flying our flag, determined to do Singapore, their families and themselves proud in their campuses.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Egypt, like Singapore, values inter-faith harmony; upholding the values of peace and mutual respect is essential in continuing to build a peaceful and harmonious Singapore.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Such acts threaten the values that Singapore revere, peace and harmony.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: We must ensure our places of worship for all faiths remain safe spaces like the rest of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: To do so, we must embrace unity in diversity.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Our mighty red dot shines bright beyond the water’s edge.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Think about how Singaporeans make our mark and add value overseas and how Singapore makes a difference in a world that we care about.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: We must carry that same pride, here on this island.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The strength of the people is in its unity. "老吾老，以及人之老".

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Care for the elders, our own and others. "Yerumbu Ora Kalluum Theiyum".

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: We must build it, we must move forward with it, together.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim, I think you have joined the rare group of Members who used all four languages in her speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Housing policies are often discussed in this House.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is a topic that is important to many.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Homes are where our children grow up, develop a sense of self and identify a space that they call their own.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Homes can be a source of pride and joy for young working adults – something that they worked hard for and something that they continue to build their dreams and aspirations on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For seniors, a home can be a sanctuary giving them peace of mind in their golden years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In land scarce Singapore, the Government takes active steps to ensure that there is housing to meet the different needs of our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But there are also competing uses for land – to generate economic growth, for environment sustainability and sometimes for cultural and historical conservation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) takes its development and stewardship role over land use seriously and undertakes this in partnership with our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In June this year, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) released the Draft Master Plan 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It was developed through URA's most extensive public engagement exercise to date with 200,000 people engaged.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We laid out our urban planning vision for the next decade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to bring jobs closer to homes and strengthen three economic gateways in the north, east and west.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to develop exciting and attractive neighbourhoods for both public and private housing, for example, in central locations, like Berlayar: regional job centres, like Woodlands; and sites closer to nature, like Kranji.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also set aside more spaces for recreation with the development of new integrated developments, new parks and park connectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Singapore will continue to be an exciting and endearing place to work, live and play.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As we develop these plans, we will not lose sight of our fundamental commitment to our people, that the Government will continue to provide affordable and accessible housing to our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This was the founding ethos for HDB, which was established in 1960, five years before Singapore's Independence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our home ownership policies give our citizens a stake in our nation, foster a sense of rootedness and a shared sense of identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will now speak about, one, how we will continue to meet the housing aspirations of Singaporeans through affordable and accessible housing; how we will plan major new estates so that new residents can move in with greater convenience and comfort; and three, how we will rejuvenate our homes and estates to make them safe, liveable and vibrant for residents of all ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the last term of Government, the pandemic impacted construction and led to delays in the completion of housing projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Application rates for BTO flats were high, waiting times were longer and resale prices increased as more buyers turned to resale flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together with industry partners, the Government responded swiftly to the situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We completed the flats delayed by COVID-19, ramped up supply of new flats, brought down waiting times and introduced multiple rounds of cooling measures to moderate the resale market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: After COVID-19, there continues to be strong broad-based housing demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Singaporeans want to start their own families with most young people getting married at about 30 years old and they want to have their own flats then.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are also singles who want to live independently, though near their family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are also seniors who want to age-in-place or right-size their housing for retirement needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In this term of Government, HDB will continue to build more, build faster and build better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to help more Singaporeans meet their housing aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also sustain a steady private housing supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: New estates will be developed in more central locations, such as Newton and Pearl's Hill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As we build more, build faster and build better, there will be greater capacity to meet the aspirations of more Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Henry Kwek spoke for some of these groups, like young Singaporeans doing well at work and earning more but are afraid that they will bust the HDB income ceiling and end up not being eligible for a HDB flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Another group of Singaporeans who desire to own their HDB flats are singles who can only apply for a BTO flat after reaching the age of 35.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In recent years, we have made significant moves to enhance singles' access to HDB flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These include expanding access to two-room flexi BTO flats island-wide, increasing the housing grant for singles and giving priority to singles when they apply to live with or near their parents for mutual care and support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We understand that there is still unmet demand from some singles who wish to apply for a BTO flat before reaching the age of 35.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Besides improving accessibility, we will also ensure that HDB flats remain affordable for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government will continue to price BTO flats so that they are affordable for buyers with different income levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes first-time buyers who may also be eligible for additional housing grants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Unlike other countries where public housing is targeted at the lower-income, almost 80% of Singapore residents stay in HDB flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We must, therefore, provide a range of BTO flats at different locations and price levels to cater to buyers with different incomes and aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Take a young couple earning around $5,000 monthly adding up to our median household income of $10,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The average price for a standard four-room flat in a July exercise was around $460,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If they opted for a four-room flat in Prime areas in this particular July exercise, given the additional subsidies for Prime flats, the couple will still be able to afford such flats with up to $350 payable in cash per month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Their mortgage servicing ratio would increase to 27% but this is still below international benchmarks of 30%-35% for affordable housing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To add, as the couple only starts paying their loan when the flat is completed, their incomes will likely have increased in those three or four years when they are waiting for the flat, so their actual mortgage servicing ratio and monthly cash outlay would be even lower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Let us consider another couple with a lower combined income of $6,000 which places them in the lower-third of households by income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the same July BTO exercise, three-room flats were going from $267,000 up to $389,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This couple would be able to afford any three-room flat only using CPF, without any cash outlay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That gives them some buffer to cover their daily expenses and build up their finances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In fact, because of the additional grants they receive, this couple would also be able to afford the average standard four-room flat in this exercise without any cash outlay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I have taken the July launch as an example, as this is the nearest launch to date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The exact prices and locations will vary across launches but our commitment is to ensure a range of options to meet diverse budgets and diverse needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also ensure that standard flats continue to form a significant portion of our annual supply to provide sufficient options for buyers with tighter budgets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And across flat types, BTOs will be priced well below comparable resale flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On top of that, we provide further means-tested grants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is a good gauge of their lived experience of affordability, as this captures how they can manage their mortgage and daily living expenses relative to their disposable income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will now touch on the resale market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As we all know, resale prices are agreed between buyers and sellers, influenced by supply and demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Behind every resale flat transaction, there is a willing buyer and a willing seller.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Buyers pay a higher price compared to BTO flats, but they get the resale flat immediately and can choose their preferred flat attributes, like location and size.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There will be resale flats with attractive attributes that allow them to command higher prices, such as being in Prime locations, on a high floor, facing a good view, near amenities and transport nodes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But there are also resale flats available at lower prices in many locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A four-room resale flat with at least 40 years remaining on the lease can go for less than $700,000 in locations, like Tampines and Punggol; less than $600,000 in Sembawang and Yishun; and less than $550,000 in Jurong West and Woodlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Before COVID-19, resale prices fell for six consecutive years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When prices rose in the COVID-19 years, we had to implement four rounds of cooling measures, such as reducing the Loan-to-Value limit for HDB housing loans and the wait-out periods for private property owners wishing to purchase HDB flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are now seeing moderation in resale price growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The quarter-on-quarter resale price index Resale Price Index growth for the last quarter at 0.9% is the lowest since the second quarter of 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are signs to point towards continued moderation in resale prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More BTO flats will reach their Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) from 2026 onwards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The increase in the supply of resale flats will help to moderate resale prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the same time, the ramp-up in BTO supply that I spoke about earlier will also help to reduce demand in the resale market, as more buyers turn to BTO flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together, these trends of increased supply and reduced demand will help support a more balanced and sustainable resale market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To sum up this section of my speech, we will keep public housing affordable and accessible for buyers with diverse needs and budgets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The robust supply of public housing will enable us to expand access to more groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ramping up housing supply also means that we will be developing in new areas, such as Tengah in the West, and Kranji in the North.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These areas present opportunities to design thoughtful and beautiful towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We did this with "Punggol 21" since the 1990s, and we are doing this again with Tengah – our first large-scale smart and sustainable town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the same time, we hear feedback from residents that amenities such as cooked food options and childcare centres were not available when they first moved in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Having been in Punggol for the past decade, I can understand how residents feel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The committee has studied the experience of residents in new large-scale BTO estates, such as Punggol and Tengah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will share more in the months to come, but today, I would like to give you a broad overview of the improvements that we are looking into, to prepare for other large-scale BTO projects we are building.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The inter-agency committee is looking into a wide variety of issues, such as transport accessibility, construction disamenities and also, mobile signal strength.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the interest of time, I will highlight three areas that HDB is working on: sheltered linkways, childcare and food options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Residents desire shelter to connect them on their commute and journeys around the neighbourhood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For new estates, from the onset, we will see how we can connect our residents to more bus stops and shop clusters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This can potentially be implemented at the BTO construction stage, especially if there are cost savings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, we know through experience that operators are hesitant to open their shops or stalls when footfall may be low in the initial period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, we already provide a rent-free period to tide operators through this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are studying how to enhance such measures while studying alternatives for residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will work with the food and retail industry to see how residents can be better served during the move-in period and the town's early years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the National Day Rally this year, the Prime Minister had shared our vision for the new BTO estates in places like Kranji, Sembawang and Woodlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They are to be well-connected to job centres in the northern region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is an opportunity to apply this resident-centric planning approach and build a new generation of heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Across Government agencies, we will plan and coordinate much more closely so that new residents enjoy greater convenience from the time they move in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to gather feedback from residents, grassroots leaders and community leaders, and adopt a resident-centric approach in planning, development and execution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our commitment is not just to new homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are equally focused on rejuvenating our mature heartlands where many Singaporeans have lived for decades.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We often hear residents asking what will happen to their flats and estates as the infrastructure, and they themselves, get older.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I assure residents that we will continue to work with you and your Town Councils to keep your homes and neighbourhoods safe, liveable and well-maintained.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many residents of flats aged around 30 years have already benefited from programmes, such as the Home Improvement Programme (HIP), covering essentials like toilets, doors and spalling concrete.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Works will be more comprehensive, using updated technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will announce more details about HIP II next year, but I will share one example today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As buildings age, the problem of water seepage becomes more common and this damages concrete.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I have seen the use of this technology and how it can help to resolve more complex water seepage cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB is currently exploring how to scale up its use in a cost-effective manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond individual flats, we will continue to refresh the whole estate, through programmes such as Remaking Our Heartlands and the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, under Remaking Our Heartlands in Choa Chu Kang, the Teck Whye and Keat Hong Shopping Centres are getting a fresh revamp, so that residents do not have to travel into town, but can enjoy themselves at the nearby malls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Outside the town centres, there will be new pocket parks, playgrounds and linkways, down to simple improvements to the lighting and seating.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Residents of private housing estates, including seniors, will not be left out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are extending these upgrading efforts to selected private housing estates, under the Estate Upgrading Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   As society ages, we have to make HDB flats and neighbourhoods more senior-friendly, to support seniors to age-in-place and remain active.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We believe that our whole society benefits when seniors live joyful, healthy and active lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes grab bars and handrails, slip-resistant flooring, wall-mounted shower seats and widened bathroom entrances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: All this will support seniors who wish to age-in-place, surrounded by familiar faces and places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But there will also be seniors who wish to monetise their flats, and find a smaller flat that suits their retirement needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Community Care Apartments combine senior-friendly design, eldercare services and activity spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have seen positive response and feedback, and we are expanding this model to more sites.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will work with MOH to provide more details when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to make Singapore an endearing home for all ages. : Sir, during this debate, we have seen many MPs speak passionately about issues concerning national development – their estates, residents, our social fabric and the environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I sincerely thank our Members for raising concerns and proposals on behalf of your residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hear you and we will continue to engage you and work with you to further improve our policies and schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To our residents, we hear your hopes and concerns, whether you are a young couple planning to start a family, a homeowner wondering what is next for your estate, or a senior thinking about retirement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will build more homes across the island, with a range of housing options to cater to different needs and budgets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will plan for infrastructure and amenities in new estates, so that residents can move in with greater comfort and convenience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will rejuvenate mature homes and estates, keeping them safe, liveable and vibrant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over six decades, we have moved from the urgent task of housing a young nation to a nation of homeowners, proud of our quality homes, well-designed towns and strong communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will carry this spirit and legacy, meet the needs of today and fulfil our aspirations for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together, let us build a Singapore that is home for all, for today and for generations to come.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Louis Chua, you have a clarification to make.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just a quick clarification for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I just wanted to ask what are these right conditions that she mentioned in her speech, whether it is certain indicators or macroeconomic factors, or some factors that MND is considering, before taking the action to review the age?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Because on the supply and demand side: demand, we do know that there is; and on supply, I think that is something within MND's control.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Singles are a very important part of our society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Because a flat that we allocate to one particular segment of the society means, unfortunately, one flat less to allocate to another segment of the society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I would say that what we are very focused on right now is to build as quickly as we can.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling, you have a clarification?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But I can sense the new resolve to tackle the challenges ahead, come what may, and to keep this miracle of Singapore going.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: There will be new stresses and anxieties and Singaporeans will need to adjust and adapt in a fast-changing and more unsettling environment.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: At the same time, we must double down in our efforts to sustain social mobility as well as protecting the vulnerable among us.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And through it all, we can build a stronger social compact and a truly "we" mindset.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: These are among the areas of priorities outlined by the President on behalf of the Government, which I fully support.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Much has been said in the last five days and so for my speech today, I would just focus on two sticky perennial issues, which I would like to add my voice to.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I raise both these issues, not because I feel that the Government has not done enough but rather these two issues: cost and jobs, are and will be an unending challenge for Singapore and would, therefore, require continued resolves to tackle them.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: How can we better moderate cost increases in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: As a tiny resource-scarce city state, where we import almost everything that we need and where our economy is constantly on an overdrive mode, Singapore is inherently more susceptible to price increases than other economies.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is a circumstance that we have to constantly manage and live with.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Like almost every economy in the world, the universal approach is to let market forces determine allocations with the use of price as a way to sort out demand and supply.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This is by far the most sensible way and it has worked this way for centuries.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: However, in Singapore's circumstances, prices tend to be more upside elastic because of our greater scarcity, as we do not readily have excess capacity to just ramp up supply where demand are high to moderate price increases.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: At the same time, due to our remarkable economic progress over the decades, there is a wider disparity now in purchasing power among our consumers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: There are people or businesses who are prepared to pay up a lot more or bid higher than others and some in the range of extreme outliers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: We see some of that in the Certificate of Entitlement bidding, where supply is limited and hence, prices is the key determinant to allocate the limited number of certificates.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Among them the core areas that the Government has committed heavy subsidies are housing, healthcare, education, transport and others.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: These direct subsidies require substantial and continual fiscal resource to fund and, hence, we must be able to keep generating revenue on a sustainable basis to pay for these items.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Fortunately, our strong economic and fiscal fundamentals avail us the Singapore dollar as a broad-base tool to mitigate inflation.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But there is a limit as to how much the strong Singapore dollar can strengthen without impacting our export competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, we do have to count on other supporting measures.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: At the same time, domestically, we are also in this necessary transition to uplift wages of fellow Singaporeans, especially the lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This has added cost pressures to businesses and some of which show up in the form of higher prices in products and services.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Also, we have also seen land costs increasing fairly steeply in recent years as Singapore continues to command premiums as a business destination and also a much sought-after residential home.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The Government has introduced a series of property cooling measures like Additional Buyers Stamp Duties, among others.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: These are all necessary to cool the market.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But besides the indirect measures, we would also need both broad-base and targeted direct measures to assist Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But we know that such direct assistances cannot be a norm and sometime down the road it has to taper down and wind down, and the pace will depend on the inflationary situation and our fiscal headroom.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: We, therefore, need to look into more supply-side measures to lower our overall cost structure in Singapore, both through administrative means as well as through improving efficiency as an economic system.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I will attempt to share some illustrative examples, not exhaustive by any means.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: While we largely leave to the spontaneity of businesses to evolve the ecosystem, it will also require the Government’s hand, from time to time, to curate, monitor and call out unfair market behaviour to protect consumers' interest.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Besides the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore, the Consumers Association of Singapore and other consumers’ advocacy groups, MPs have also played a part in the past to call out anti-competitive practices.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: For example, Parliamentary Questions were raised in the past when we saw retail petrol prices lagging on the downside but quicker to rise on the upside.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The cost of, for example, repairing seepages in HDB flats has increased significantly.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The problem with seepages in buildings is that you cannot really see where the source of leak is with the naked eye.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, there is often some amount of guesswork by the repair contractor.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: When a seepage is reported during a raining day, the contractor would wait for a dry day to carry out the repair.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: After the repair, the contractor would wait for the next rainy day to determine if the seepage repair has been effective.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: If it is not, they would find another dry day to repair on another suspected spot.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, for more difficult and complex seepage situations, the process may go on for a few rounds to the frustrations of residents, who has to bear the inconveniences of multiple appointments and continued seepages.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Typically, what the contractors would do is to carry out what they call "PU injection", injecting high pressure liquid, polyurethane (PU) chemical, into the suspected cracks in concrete structures hoping that these PUs will plug the gaps and source of the leaks.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It would be too much to ask for these companies to invest in costly sophisticated technology to more precisely diagnosed the root causes of seepages, not knowing that they can still win the next contract or next tender.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, I hope HDB or Building Construction Authority can intervene to find an industry solution.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: We almost need an Industry Transformation Map of sorts to invest in the research, technology, training so as to improve on the way we can diagnose the source of the seepage.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This would help contractors to better able and more accurately repair the seepages in older flats and hence, costing less.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Another cause of concern that I would like to raise is the extreme high bids we saw in heartland shop spaces.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Such record-high bids, though not the norm, nevertheless, has the effect of setting new reference benchmarks and may influence future would-be bidders to submit higher bids, leading to upside stickiness in pricing.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Other private HDB shops landlord may use this new higher benchmark reference to price up when they renew the rental.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: While we leave it to markets forces to determine prices, we must drill down if such outlier bids are sustainable in business, and the impact to healthcare costs at the neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: There must also be a so-called price reasonableness assessment.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Hopefully that will help reduce future occurrences of overly high rental bids.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Another case in point is the high rental bid for hawker centres.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This is way higher than the $1,800 median successful tender price for cooked food stalls in 2023.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Again, this may not be the norm, but it could create upside headroom for rental prices to escalate.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Let us see if this new model works, but I hope that NEA can, in addition, also consider the PQM approach that HDB has adopted.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Another measure that I hope HDB can consider and look into is to increase the supply of rental spaces in locations where rental bids tend to be high, as the high rental bids may well be due to inadequate retail spaces in high population-density residential town.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Prior to the Government's decision to resume building of hawker centres, coffee shops were at one point changing hands in the tens of millions of dollars.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But with the hawker centres being built and new supply of retail stalls, we have seen transaction prices of coffeeshops stabilised.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, this is something that if we supply, it can make a difference.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I have noticed that in Hong Kong, among the most expensive commercial real estate area, like Central and the Admiralty areas, there will always be side lanes in between the top-grade office properties, where low costs budget retail shops can co-exist.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: These are the small retail shops when we can find, among the buildings, where you see Hong Kong cafes, or "cha chan teng", selling affordable meal sets, small sundry shops selling low-cost daily grocery items and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: If the prices or rents of these spaces at these small lanes are to be benchmarked against the valuations of the adjacent premium office buildings, the retail shops would not be able to survive at the affordable prices that they provide.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, perhaps, URA and the Singapore Land Authority can study what administrative measures do the Hong Kong land authority has to allow such dispensation.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I know we do have such similar dispensation of sorts where we set aside office spaces in commercial buildings for non-profit use that are for social and community good.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I always thought it would be a great idea for Marina Bay to also have a social enterprise-run hawker centre.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: That would be helpful to the office workers there who wish to have an affordable meal.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In this year’s National Day Rally speech, the Prime Minister mentioned jobs as a main focus.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: At one juncture, he repeated “jobs, jobs, jobs” three times in succession.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Despite Singapore having among the lowest unemployment rate in the world and, in fact, we have to count on foreign labour to fill up many of jobs not taken up by Singaporeans, it is very heartening to hear this from the top-of-the-house leadership.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It demonstrates once again that when it comes to unemployment, we set very low thresholds of tolerance and we are determined not to leave any jobseekers behind.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And that determination is manifested in the whole gamut of policies and the resources the Government has put in place to create jobs to sustain employability.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: On the demand side, the priority is to grow the economy.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: On the supply side, the unrelenting endeavor to equip and upskill Singaporeans to take on job opportunities across life stages, starting in schools, during their career life span and even during their senior years.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: We have done much on either side, the demand and the supply.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The part that I hope we do better is how we can match the demand to supply, so that we can see more meaningful employment outcomes.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Imagine the stresses and anxieties, as well as the emotional toil and frustrations having to send countless CVs, going for interviews, awaiting outcomes, only to be disappointed again.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It saddens me when I see middle-aged PMETs with good work experience, still able, still capable, but having to retire early or to be not meaningfully employed.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This is especially so, when now, today, we have our life expectancies, health expectancies are also all increasing.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Very often, the skills and experiences that these mid-career PMETs have are actually the skills that the companies are looking for.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But, somehow, the match just does not occur.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Some of these available jobs are quite general in nature.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Some administrative, it could be support roles; some are managerial, which we have no shortage of experienced managers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, it is not due to the lack of jobs or not lack of skills or experiences, then what are the impediments?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Mismatched expectations; bias, whether is it age or others; inability of the jobseekers to impress the hirers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Singaporeans, some of us may tend to undersell ourselves.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Here, I would just want to focus on one particular impediment and, that is, the jobseekers are not being plugged into the employers' hiring network.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The companies may still advertise the jobs on public platforms if they are opening their search to include foreign candidates, as part of MOM requirements.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: How do we better match jobs, especially for more senior PMET positions?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Thirdly, HR managers and HR search firms are the critical conduits, and they must be similarly aligned as well in terms of giving candidates that come from outside their network a chance to be interviewed, for example, and to help the company grow the local core.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The jobseekers must have the adaptive and positive mindset to ride through the job search journey and be well-aware and realistic of the changing market landscape.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: At the policy level, we must resolve to leave no jobseekers behind and help every Singaporeans who wish to be gainfully employed, find their livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I have seen extreme volatilities in markets, very often to the detriment of economies and societies.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And I know too well that markets do misbehave from time to time.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It may not always bring us to the right place that we desire and that is why often we see central banks and governments intervene to steer the markets to the right pricing.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: We must endeavour to keep cost and prices stable for reasons of our economic competitiveness and affordability, and also to do our best to help every jobseeker find the best opportunity so that they can also live fulfilled lives and take care of their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In the past few months at NTUC, I have focused my work on these two areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: On supporting our senior workers, let me put on record, a big thanks to brother Heng Chee How, who has been supporting and championing our senior workers for the last two decades on behalf of NTUC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Now that he has retired as the most senior labour MP by age, or maybe not the most senior, other than the Secretary-General, I thought I should step in to continue the good work he has done by championing our senior workers for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Personally, I have also hit two senior milestones very recently: one, becoming eligible to withdraw from my CPF; and two, most proudly welcoming a new daughter-in-law into our family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: More importantly, I have always cared deeply about our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I have advocated for many senior residents in Pasir Ris and now I feel very honoured to have the chance to engage a wider and broader segment of senior workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Listening to their stories, understanding their struggles and also sharing in their aspirations inspire me to do more for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: On the AI front, I have spent the last year diving into this technological wonderland, taking many courses, experimenting with the 10-over AI tools that I have downloaded on my mobile phone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: My mission: to learn as fast as I can to drive NTUC's digitalisation efforts and to support business' transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I have been visiting many technology companies and attending AI events, which felt like an intense SkillsFuture boot camp, in the last couple of months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: So, initially, I planned to speak on these two tech topics separately, but as I reflected more deeply, it dawned on me.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Ageing and AI should not be mutually exclusive or stand alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In fact, they could form a powerful partnership, and that is the idea I want to explore with us here today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Singapore is being shaped by two major shifts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I refer to them as the two AIs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: AI, number one, we are familiar, it is artificial intelligence; and AI, number two, ageing individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: One generates rapid knowledge, the other brings accumulated wisdom.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: And as the saying goes, knowledge can inform us what is the quickest path up a mountain, but it is wisdom.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Wisdom is knowing if the mountain is even worth climbing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: AI number one gives us answers very quickly; but wisdom from AI number two helps us to ask the right questions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We can either learn to ride them or risk being swept away.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For many senior workers, let us face it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Productivity slows, knowledge and technology kept on evolving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But AI can complement our senior workers by giving very updated information and analysis at lightning speed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: On the other hand, AI may be game changing, but we also know that it can hallucinate and lead to information overload.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Our seniors with years of experience and wisdom can guide the use of AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The real opportunity lies in bringing these two AIs together, to redefine the future of Singapore's workforce as one that is smarter, more inclusive and future-ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: So, let us take a look at what are the challenges that our senior workers face today and what more can we do to support them?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But as our workforce ages rapidly, we must do more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: That is why in last year’s Budget speech, I urged employers to see mid-career workers beyond their age; to hire more of them; to pay them fairly, based on their skills and experience; to give protected time for their training; and recognise their acquired skillsets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: If left unaddressed, age-related bias could discourage labour force participation among senior workers, resulting in a loss of valuable experience in our workforce and institutional knowledge, and worsening Singapore’s manpower challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Yet, amid these challenges lies a powerful opportunity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Ageing should not be seen as a liability but as a source of strength.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Research, including findings from Harvard Health, shows that older workers often make more rational decisions and demonstrate better judgement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Employers must recognise that this kind of expertise, accumulated from years of experience, is essential for navigating uncertainty and making better business decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: It is timely for us now to take a fresh look at how we can better support our senior workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: From our engagements, broadly, there are three archetypes of senior workers who need further support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: There are those who wish to extend their retirement age and to work for as long as they are healthy and possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: There are those who would like to slow down, maybe have some flexibility to contribute back meaningfully to the workplace and to society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: There is also a group who finds it very difficult to re-enter the workforce when they lose their jobs and they need targeted support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: So, let me share two real-life encounters that I had over the last couple of weeks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: At one of the Tripartite Work Group dialogues, I met a gentleman in his 50s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: While actively looking for a job, he is also having to look after his elderly parents-in-law and support their children through their tertiary education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Even after lowering his salary expectations, his applications have not been successful, and we are still supporting him.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Recently, I met Ms Lim Kai Ning, the young co-founder of Courage Chapter, a startup that helps senior professionals transition into their next chapter through meaningful projects and roles that tap into their skills and experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Her journey began not with a business plan, but with a rather deep, personal experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Her father retired nine years ago in his 50s and like many, he looked forward to a well-deserved rest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But just six months into retirement, he felt less engaged and contemplating a strong desire to contribute back to the society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: He wanted more balance in his life and decided to work part-time while pursuing his hobbies, and today, he teaches three days a week at a local university and advises on operations for a friend’s F&B business and is more fulfilled than ever.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: This experience inspired Kai Ning to start Courage Chapter, to help other seniors tap into their wealth of experience while enjoying flexible work arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The courage to work should be celebrated and we can do more to scale these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: As industries transform, our senior workers should be given fair access to training and upskilling opportunities so they can adapt and continue contributing meaningfully.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We have heard a lot from Members in this Chamber and we are also hearing concerns from workers, particularly in white-collar professions across sectors in ICT, in finance and media, and even freelancers about their anxiety over job security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Globally, we witnessed labour disputes arising from the adoption of AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Last year, I spoke about the Hollywood Writers’ Guild Association and this year, in fact, the SAG-Aftra video games actors were on strike that only ended in July 2025 after a year-long protest against AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: At NTUC, our response to AI is not to protect jobs from disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Instead, our vision is to help our workers to thrive in the AI economy, by ensuring a just transition, supporting business transformation and upskilling our workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Just as we lifted workers through the computer revolution in the 1980s, the rise of Internet in the 2000s, we will ensure that no worker will be left behind, including and especially, all our senior workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For example, SBS Transit used the CTC Grant to implement an AI-powered tyre management system, turning a manual process into a digitalised, predictive one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: This significantly reduced man-hours and enabled technicians to do higher-value jobs, improving their wages and job prospects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Brother Mazri bin Masrah, a 52-year-old technician, successfully transitioned through this AI transformation in SBS Transit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: After spending about 18 years as a driver, he became a bus technician and completed a work-study diploma sponsored by SBS Transit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: He was then selected to be a diagnostic expert, a new career scheme developed by SBS Transit to upskill their technician workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: With structured training, he now uses AI-powered tools, like the automated Tyre Management System, to boost productivity and sharpen his technical skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: His journey shows how older workers can thrive in a tech-enabled environment with the right support and opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: At the Ong Teng Cheong Labour Leadership Institute, we are piloting an AI research assistant to streamline research and in future, maybe even curriculum design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: One affected key staff is Ms Ng Yuen Jiuan, or we know her affectionately as Jiuan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
