text: Whether it is in preschool education, youth development, worker upskilling, supporting businesses, addressing the cost of living, or helping young parents and the sandwich generation, or caring for seniors and in providing humanitarian support such as in Gaza as shared by Member Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I may have missed it, but I did not hear anyone calling for less to be done.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Some Members cautioned against “growing GDP at all costs.” From the speeches heard here, this is not what anyone is advocating.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: It is the means by which we create resources to care for every member of our society.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: By enlarging opportunity and walking this journey together, we give every generation not just hope, but the confidence that tomorrow will be a better day than today.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: With a larger pie, it brings me to the fourth theme that was common across all the speeches, on how to distribute the pie fairly.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Mr Fadli Fawzi reminded us of the dangers of meritocracy, where some may be left behind.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar and Mr Xie Yao Quan stressed that while meritocracy is not perfect, in Ms Mariam’s words, "We must continue to refine it, to strengthen it and to make sure meritocracy in Singapore remains fair and real – not just in principle, but in practice." As our Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said, "we cannot stand still" and we must "tilt the balance continually" to keep society fair.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: As Ms Mariam Jaafar, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Goh Hanyan, Mr Darryl David, Mr Gerald Giam and Mr David Hoe have highlighted, our youths may begin from different starting points, but we must ensure that they all have equal opportunities to succeed.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Some Members reminded us that success cannot be measured by GDP or wealth alone, but by ensuring every Singaporean has the chance to move up.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: True success means that a child born into a less advantaged family can still aspire, work hard and achieve his or her dreams.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Recognising different starting points, many MPs defined success as those with less must be given more to ensure equal opportunity.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I do hope mountain biking and cycling is considered too.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Success must also be measured in the well-being of families and communities: affordable housing, accessible healthcare and the dignity of work.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Success in Singapore must be more than individual achievement.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: It must be a collective, where communities thrive together, when those with less are given more and when every Singaporean has the opportunity to live a fulfilling life.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi shared "we first" as a powerful enabler that can strengthen cohesion and bolster unity and this is the cornerstone of a caring and values-driven society.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Something which Dr Charlene Chen shared where kindness must be lived in every sphere of life. "We first" means a society that strives for a collective good, not self-interest even as we recognise differences.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Our commitment to "we first" will always be tested.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The recent incident of suspicious parcels sent to places of worship reminds us that there will always be those who try to magnify our differences and sow division.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The only way forward is for us to stay strong, deepen our solidarity and care for one another, building a Singapore where every citizen belongs.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: It has been ingrained in us from the beginning.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: As other speakers had previously shared, our Malay/Muslim community continues to excel – whether in terms of education, employability, or our professionals who now receive recognition on the world stage.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: However, this effort is still ongoing and there is so much more that we can achieve together.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: All these could not be accomplished through individual achievement alone.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: It stems from community support that constantly helps one another.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: At the grassroots level, many volunteers in our Malay/Muslim community also contribute their time and energy.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: In my previous speech, I also shared how students from Muhammadiyah Welfare Home were able to learn robotics through guidance from engineers in our professional networks.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: This is what "we first" is all about – a community that puts the collective good above all else, instead of just self-interest.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Let us continue to work together to build a more caring, more empowered and more united community.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, allow me to draw the threads together as we head towards the end.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: This is the very foundation of Singapore’s survival and progress.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Second, while transformation brings anxieties, it also carries hope.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Every segment of society – youths, workers, persons with disabilities, seniors, families, businesses and even our natural environment – has representation in this Chamber.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: To be inclusive, we must continue to make these voices heard.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: It is the means by which we create resources to care for every member of our society.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Fifth, we have already embraced and must continue to embrace the different definitions of success, beyond grades or income, to include dignity, opportunity and quality of life.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: And lastly, that all this is anchored on "we first", the conviction that progress must be shared, and Singapore is strongest when we stand together.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Let us respond with courage, with care and with confidence.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Let us renew our compact, not just with words but with deeds.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Let us build a Singapore that is not only successful, but also one that is just, compassionate and united.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: A Singapore where every citizen has reason to hope, every family has reason to strive and every generation has reason to believe that tomorrow will be better than today.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I call upon all the Members of this House, on both sides of the aisle, backbenchers and frontbenchers, to join me in thanking the President for his Address.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: After five long days, I am happy to pose the following question to Members one last time.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Last month, we marked our 60th year of Independence.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: It has been a remarkable journey, for ours was an improbable beginning.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Sixty years ago, we stepped into the unknown with newfound independence – with limited resources, no hinterland of our own, no credible military to defend our borders and a population of diverse origins.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Yet with selfless sacrifice, an indomitable spirit and the resolve to come together regardless of race or religion, the Pioneer Generation laid the foundations for a strong and enduring nation.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Each generation since has built upon that legacy – embracing change, persevering through crises and weaving together diverse threads to become one nation.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The world around us is changing in profound ways.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We must choose our route wisely, craft new strategies and go forward with courage and above all, with unity.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: America is less willing to play the role of global insurer.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: This reflects not just the choices of its leadership elite, but also deeper questions within its society – about America’s ability to secure its well-being through a global system aimed at mutual gains.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The result is a more unsettled and chaotic world.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The rules and norms that helped keep the peace and enabled rising living standards globally are losing force.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Acts of aggression, coercion, or unreasonable demands are now more readily tolerated, and even appeased.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Meanwhile, the weaponisation of trade and economic interdependence has made international relations more fraught and complex than ever.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Each is determined to tilt the balance of power in its favour and to draw others into its orbit.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: This rivalry will shape the strategic environment for decades to come.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: These are not transient headwinds, but fundamental shifts in the tides.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The seas ahead will be rougher and far less predictable than before.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: By charting our course with quiet confidence and resolve, we can shape our own destiny.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We can never take our security for granted, especially in an era when tensions can flare up suddenly, in the region and globally.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We have long invested steadily in our defence, knowing that ultimately, we can only depend on ourselves for our security.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: What began as a matter of dire necessity has become part of our ethos.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We will continue to strengthen our capabilities, counter emerging threats – from cybersecurity to hybrid warfare – and support our National Servicemen, who form the backbone of our defence.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: It is also about withstanding new and unconventional challenges.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Foreign actors will seek to influence domestic public opinion to advance their own agendas.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: They will use every means – from social media to traditional platforms – to spread disinformation, seed discord and cause rifts in our society.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We must therefore equip Singaporeans to discern fact from fiction, understand and uphold our national interests and resist external manipulation from near and far.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Equally, we must guard against dangers at home – from acts of terrorism to scams and to drugs in all their forms, including vapes now laced with harmful substances.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: These are not just law enforcement issues; they threaten the harmony, trust and confidence that underpin our society.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Each of us must play our part in fortifying our home.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Through new approaches to Total Defence and National Education, and by creating more ways for Singaporeans to contribute, we will strengthen our resilience as one people.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: At the same time, we will play a constructive role in efforts to shape a fair and stable global order in the years ahead.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We will contribute to deeper Association for Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) integration, support reforms to ensure effective multilateralism at the United Nations and World Trade Organisation, and deepen our partnerships with like-minded nations to preserve and open-up flows of trade and investment.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: By standing with our friends and partners, we amplify our collective voice and enhance our influence.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: It generates the resources needed to secure our future and improve lives.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We cannot match other countries in size or scale.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: But we can compete on speed, ingenuity and trust.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: In a more fragmented world, Singapore must remain a safe harbour: a reliable base from which to navigate global complexities, and a gateway to Asia’s dynamism.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Global competition is intensifying, as the major economies seek to re-shore or near-shore key investments.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Yet competing on costs alone will not work.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The work has begun and it will go deep into the issues that matter most.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Much effort will be required to restructure industries and build deeper capabilities in every sector of the future – from advanced manufacturing to information technology (IT) and finance, to clean energies and environmental sustainability.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Above all, we must foster an outgoing and experimental spirit among our enterprises and people.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: It is how we can grow leading firms and secure good jobs and rising incomes for Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The trust built through many years of tripartism gives us an edge.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: It enables us to move faster in deploying new technologies like artificial intelligence (AI), while managing disruptions to the workforce and generating new job opportunities.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Most firms know of AI, but few have embarked on serious transformation.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: In this way, AI can be used both to raise efficiency and to complement human abilities, so that the gains are shared broadly and we involve all Singaporeans in building new sources of competitiveness.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Technology will also be crucial in helping us tackle existential threats like climate change.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We will invest in new technologies for decarbonisation and coastal protection, and support enterprises developing breakthrough environmental solutions.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We will also press ahead with partnerships to develop a robust carbon credits market and mobilise finance for sustainable infrastructure in the region.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: In doing so, we strengthen Singapore’s resilience while contributing to the sustainability of our region and the world.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Our ambition is clear: to make Singapore a place where ideas can take root and where entrepreneurs can build, innovate, expand abroad and become regional and global leaders in their respective fields.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Equally, our goal is to ensure that this progress uplifts everyone.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We seek not just growth, but inclusive growth – a society where every citizen shares in the nation’s prosperity and every Singaporean has the confidence that tomorrow will bring brighter opportunities and a better life.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Jobs and skills will keep evolving, faster than before.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Old industries will fade and new ones will emerge.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Skills that are in demand today may become obsolete tomorrow.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We cannot hold back this tide of change.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: But we can prepare ourselves – individually and collectively – to navigate it with confidence.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: These efforts reflect our conviction that Singaporeans should never face uncertainty on their own.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Through Forward Singapore, we have strengthened our assurances to Singaporeans at every stage of life, so that every individual can live with dignity, purpose and hope.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: And we will keep building on this in the years ahead.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: No one will have to walk the journey alone.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: For our youths: we will prepare them for a future that will be different – helping them secure good jobs, easing their anxieties and equipping them with the skills to thrive in a changing world.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Beyond this, we will give them a stronger voice in shaping the Singapore they want, for they will be the co-authors of, and must own, our nation’s next chapter.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: For our families: we will keep public housing affordable and accessible.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: But we know families are also stretched in caring for both the young and old.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We will therefore enhance support for caregivers, including through more flexible work arrangements and a stronger ecosystem of care in the community.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: For our seniors: we will be a place where every citizen can have a joyful and fulfilling life as they age.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We will encourage and support those who wish to continue working, so their experience and wisdom can benefit others.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: For those looking to retire, we will do more to help them build a nest egg, so they can live their golden years with renewed purpose and peace of mind.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We also recognise the immediate pressures of daily living.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Rising costs – driven by global conflicts, tariffs and supply chain disruptions – weigh heavily on households.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: That is why we will continue to cushion these burdens and ensure that every citizen has access to life’s essentials.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: But our aim goes beyond helping Singaporeans to cope with uncertainty.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Every citizen should have the confidence that, whatever lies ahead, they can pursue their aspirations and provide for their families.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: By strengthening assurance and keeping opportunities open, we will build resilience and confidence as a society even in an uncertain world.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: As societies mature, wealth can entrench and inequality can become self-perpetuating.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Privilege is passed down, while disadvantage becomes harder to escape.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We cannot allow this trend to be ingrained in Singapore.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We must actively resist it and find practical ways to narrow the gap.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We have worked hard to ensure fairer outcomes and we have made progress.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Wages are rising, especially for those in the lowest 20%.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Our home ownership rate remains the world’s highest, even for lower-income households.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We must keep social mobility alive with each new generation.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: This has always been a national priority and it remains our shared ambition for the future.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Everyone must have the chance to move up the escalator of skills, confidence and a better life.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Every Singaporean must be given the opportunity to develop themselves to their fullest potential.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: By investing from the early years onwards, we will give every Singaporean the best possible start in life.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: It continues through our education system, which opens up multiple pathways to success, develops good character and values, and celebrates different forms of excellence.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Beyond academic abilities, we must equally value technical expertise, creative flair, practical problem-solving skills, and sporting and artistic virtuosity.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: At work, we will enhance training and career pathways so that Singaporeans can excel and be recognised for their achievements across a wide range of skills and professions.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: This requires us to challenge deep-seated assumptions about what constitutes valuable work and who we consider to be professionals.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Progress means recognising the value in every job – in the trades, crafts and services, no less than in offices and boardrooms – and ensuring that everyone who contributes to society earns respect and can build a good life.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Singapore must also remain a home where the vulnerable amongst us are not only cared for with compassion but also empowered to pursue their hopes and dreams.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Ultimately, our nation’s success will never be measured by economic growth alone.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: It must be judged by how we support the vulnerable, and how we enable every Singaporean – young and old – to contribute, and to live with dignity.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: This is the promise of Singapore: that birth does not dictate destiny, that no one is left behind and that every generation can look ahead with optimism and hope.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Singapore can only stand tall if we act as one people.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: But unity is not mustered by belief alone.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We will work with community leaders to grow networks of care, such as by bringing neighbours together to support one another.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We will also create more space for citizens to take the initiative and lead ground-up programmes to take on the causes that matter.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Everyone will have a say in building our shared future.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: By creating a more open and engaged society, we will strengthen Singapore and deepen the solidarity that defines us.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We will also do more to make giving and volunteering a way of life.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Whether as individuals, community groups, or enterprises, we all have a role in building a culture of contribution – one where success is not measured only by personal achievement, but by what we do together for the common good.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: And where, by learning about each other’s circumstances of life and experiences, we enhance our sense of shared reality.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: However, a “We First” society is not only about organised programmes.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: It is equally about the values we live by, and our regular habits of care – from offering a seat on the train to lending a hand in times of need.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: They may often be simple acts, but these too are the threads that hold our social fabric together.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: In many parts of the world, social divisions are hardening.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Ethnic tensions, in particular, are rising, and the basic understandings that underpin stable, multicultural societies are being eroded.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: What makes Singapore exceptional is our unity – built not despite our diversity, but by embracing it and finding richness in our different cultures.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We should resist any temptation to use race or religion for political gain, or to view national issues through such lenses.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We know too well, including from our own history, the dangerous divisions and lasting scars that result from yielding to these temptations.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Instead, we must continue to nurture what makes us distinctively Singaporean: the ability to accept our varied identities, to take a respectful interest in each other’s cultures, and to build common ground through shared experiences.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We must keep evolving and deepening our approach to multiculturalism.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We do so by ensuring each of our diverse Singaporean traditions remains vibrant and refreshed with every generation.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: And importantly too, by encouraging the criss-crossing of influences that comes when Singaporeans delve into one another’s cultures.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Or like Syakirah Dahiyah Sudanto, now in her second year at Ngee Ann Polytechnic, who became its first non-Chinese student to pursue Chinese Studies.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Or Soo Mei Fei, who stumbled upon Indian classical dance in Secondary 1 and now, in her 20s, is a professional Bharatanatyam exponent.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: By both deepening our multiculturalism and enlarging our common ground, we strengthen mutual respect and grow our shared national identity.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We have valued stewardship over expediency, enduring responsibility over transient gain.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: As we turn the page on SG60 and write our nation’s next chapter, let us be guided by this spirit of trust.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Let us stay firm in our resolve, yet open to change; confident in our future, yet humble about our place in the world; proud of our diversity, yet united as one people.

speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: This is how we will build a better Singapore – not just for ourselves, but for our children and generations to come.
